Happy 250th, America!
I hope amidst your celebrations you took a moment to appreciate what an extraordinary country we live in.
Two hundred and fifty years sounds like a long time until you remember the universe is nearly 14 billion years old. And yet, in that astonishingly short span, the United States has become one of the most influential experiments in self-government the world has ever seen.
As we celebrate that remarkable milestone, let's look back at three defining moments from three American presidents who helped shape the country we know today.
### **Washington Walked Away From Absolute Power**
Arguably, the greatest thing Washington ever did for this country wasn't winning power (although that is obviously up there), but walking away from it.
For virtually all of recorded history, when someone won a war, they took the crown and ruled with absolute power. Great military leaders became kings and emperors. Washington had every opportunity to do exactly that and chose not to. Across Europe, the world was still ruled by monarchs.
Britain's King George III sat on the throne, and France was descending into the chaos of the French Revolution, which would eventually produce another ruler who refused to give up power: Napoleon Bonaparte. Germany wouldn't even become a unified nation until 1871, and its first democratic republic wouldn't arrive until after World War I. Most of Europe wouldn't become stable liberal democracies until the twentieth century. You get the picture. In this era, if you won power, you usually held it for life.
History offered almost no examples of leaders voluntarily walking away.
For Washington to give up power not once, but _twice_ was genuinely unheard of. And no one was better positioned to become America's king than he was. Imagine the country's most decorated military hero, biggest celebrity, and one of its richest people were all the same person. That was George Washington.

He could have easily become American royalty. Some of his officers even floated the idea after the Revolutionary War. Americans adored him. Having just won a revolution against a king, it would have been completely intuitive to replace him with another one. There could have been two King Georges on both sides of the Atlantic. Yet, Washington refused, choosing his home over a throne. More than a decade after the Declaration of Independence, the ratified Constitution created a new office unlike any the world had seen. Washington became the first person to define what an American president should be.
Then eight years later, he did something even more remarkable. After serving two terms as president, he walked away again.
The Constitution didn't set term limits. Washington simply believed that if one man held power for too long, the presidency would start to look more like a monarchy than a republic. That single decision may have done more to secure American democracy than any battle he ever fought.
For nearly a century and a half, every president followed Washington's example. It wasn't until Franklin D. Roosevelt broke the tradition during World War II that the country eventually wrote the two-term limit into the Constitution through the Twenty-second Amendment.
Washington showed the world that the true test of a free society is how the powerful choose to give it back. Every peaceful transfer of power since runs on the precedent Washington set.
### **Lincoln Held the Country Together Through Pragmatism Rooted In Principle**
Lincoln inherited a country tearing itself in half. He had to make impossible calculations about how to preserve the nation without destroying the principles it claimed to represent.
Eleven Southern states would secede and more than 600,000 Americans would die in the Civil War. Every decision Lincoln made carried unimaginable consequences.
Today Lincoln is enshrined as one of America's great saints and martyrs, his face on the penny, the five-dollar bill, an iconic marble memorial in the capital, and Mount Rushmore. But while he was president, the consensus was far less flattering. People across the political spectrum thought he was simultaneously weak, tyrannical, naive, too radical and somehow not radical enough. The obvious hero we know today was, in his own time, a guy few people had faith in.
Lincoln was attacked constantly and not just by the opposition, but by his own party. The Radical Republicans thought him hopelessly cautious, too slow to kill slavery, too eager to compromise, and by 1864 some of his own allies were openly searching for a replacement candidate.
What his critics misunderstood, though, was the very problem Lincoln was solving. The Radicals wanted him to abolish slavery immediately, in one stroke. Lincoln wanted slavery gone too, but he knew that if he moved too fast, he could lose the war and free no one.
Four slave states had stayed loyal to the Union: Kentucky, Missouri, Maryland, and Delaware. If Lincoln made the war explicitly about ending slavery too soon, those states could have bolted to the Confederacy, taking their people, territory, and strategic position with them. The Union would've lost the war if that happened.
So he couldn't just declare slavery over. He had to end it in an order that wouldn't blow up his own side. That patience is what makes the Emancipation Proclamation so brilliant. It's the moment the careful sequencing finally pays off, the place where you can see Lincoln fuse principle and pragmatism into a single act instead of choosing between them.
The Emancipation Proclamation is remembered as a moral declaration, which it was. But it was also one of the shrewdest chess moves in American history reframing the war's purpose. By making emancipation a Union war aim, Lincoln made it far harder for Britain and France, both of which had already abolished slavery, to recognize or support the Confederacy. He transformed the Civil War from a fight over secession into a fight over human freedom.
Lincoln was also deeply pluralistic in the way he governed. Instead of surrounding himself with loyalists, he appointed rivals who had run against him. He wanted the strongest people in the room, not the most agreeable ones. He did so because he needed their expertise and their political coalitions. The level of hostility he faced from within his own cabinet would be unimaginable today.

Lincoln also understood that winning the war would not automatically heal the country. His approach to Reconstruction, captured in the phrase "with malice toward none, with charity for all," was an attempt to make reunion possible rather than turn victory into permanent revenge.
He didn't live to implement it, and the years that followed exposed how fragile that vision was. Still, the framework revealed a leader thinking beyond the immediate emergency toward the long-term health of the republic.
# **Eisenhower Had the Integrity to Criticize His Own Institution**
By the time Dwight Eisenhower left office in 1961, no American had more credibility with the military. He had commanded the Allied forces behind D-Day and later served as NATO's first Supreme Allied Commander. As president, he oversaw America's rise as the dominant military power in the world. If anyone had earned the right to celebrate America's military, it was him.
Yet in his final speech as president, Eisenhower chose to warn the country about the danger of the very system he had spent his life helping to build and lead. He gave that danger a name that stuck forever: the "military-industrial complex."
That this message came from a five-star general who had helped win World War II makes it all the more remarkable. American military strength was central to his identity. He understood better than almost anyone why American strength mattered. But he also understood that even necessary institutions can become dangerous when they accumulate too much power. That kind of integrity is rarely seen. It is much easier to criticize institutions you oppose than to criticize institutions you love and helped create.
Among the highest forms of patriotism is loving your country enough to hold its institutions accountable--not because you want them to fail, but because you want them to live up to their purpose.
***
Two hundred and fifty years later, America is still an experiment. Our work is far from finished and the next chapters will require each generation to decide what it is willing to do to make it better. History is not a perfect teacher, but it does show us what courage and selfless service looks like when the stakes are the highest.

Maybe, since you opened my email, he has helped you, too.Why are Lewis’s words so powerful?It’s because he was a master at addressing life’s most important questions. His vivid language is delightful and captivating to read.Lewis’s signature ability to communicate the truth about Christianity has inspired so many skeptics to **become** believers and even more Christians to renew and deepen their faith. He is certainly the greatest Christian apologist of the twentieth century.To help you learn more about Lewis’s works related to Christianity, we produced a powerful, free course, “**C.S. Lewis on Christianity** ,” which you can now own on DVD absolutely free.**Claim your FREE DVD set of “C.S. Lewis on Christianity” using this secure link:**[ https://info.hillsdale.edu/free-cs-lewis-christianity-dvd ](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/9CSArvSIJUJNCw2gBgUNr%2BYnCRKZp0%2BU8f7NQKORQ8uBW2kaocjSWk48VnCL%0AajoOhS54AKl3mkBf99w4UGAki0nkfR%2BuhFaJ6kaSJ%2Fi%2BwTzCLmy312YVSn1w%0AIoEzTbK2wVJU%2B%2Fb6z2ej0iPWXUTGwtyWEmYTEbryL60yofDKFhQmgteylalq%0AnzJETGX9ObNOe2MjrT8y4o3Ngz%2Fjb%2FmMIA%3D%3D%0A/710883e76fd92d8d)In this course, you will study Lewis’s profound insights on the central topics of Christianity, including:
* Good and evil
* Conversion and faith
* Prayer and the Bible
* Suffering and death
* Heaven and Hell

The instructor, Michael Ward, is a distinguished visiting professor at Hillsdale College and a member of the Faculty of Theology and Religion at the University of Oxford. He wrote _Planet Narnia: The Seven Heavens in the Imagination of C.S. Lewis_ and _After Humanity: A Guide to C.S. Lewis’s The Abolition of Man_. He even spent three years living in Lewis’s Oxford home as the resident Warden of The Kilns!You’ll find this course especially moving because it examines C.S. Lewis’s beautiful writings about faith. You’ll even trace Lewis’s own journey from skeptic to believer. The combination provides an opportunity for you to grow in your knowledge and understanding of Christianity.[ So please join us in studying Christianity with C.S. Lewis and Michael Ward with this beautiful free DVD set. ](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/Rx2yTChXe5pbLlRsltL7jX9c6dl3rx11ZxB2xAsWVYJhKBs9EBzkxRNkGVub%0AU%2F%2BHtnYqESusF77gpYRgmfDi3TVSbdqskAXnhmsWipvdM159Oga7xPJla7To%0AgpZSTtcpguesnAjAp3VDpED96EXrhLdDS8TdKV3%2BUzX5wNMyHuUqdXzBVLll%0AMTOGjruK%2Bx3s7vjdbR8KrGPOARETxFozDw%3D%3D%0A/a59a09a2b9adc51d)Warm regards, Bill Gray ‘01
Vice President
Institutional Advancement
Hillsdale College **P.S.** You probably know that C.S. Lewis also wrote the children’s series, _The Chronicles of Narnia_. My wife and I read those books to our children so many times! I can’t tell you how many dog-eared copies we have of these. One of the best parts of this course is learning how the Christian faith is woven into these captivating stories. **I hope you’ll take advantage of this great FREE DVD offer today:**[ https://info.hillsdale.edu/free-cs-lewis-christianity-dvd ](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/0%2Bg7QyKjj4gQm66BFYzvi3TkXnJj9O3weEyw2fJQ16DRWkACalu4U7jMP73B%0A71cgqgWSpglucc%2Bd3tcXftVqLf%2BYNT3PjIU%2BYoFdZ254uvhgbtXJfLgCxwSF%0AYgJV9KrcQ1KaDkrzh0FFM%2B95B9OqvtLfcSaqNeoJU1lc87HCTsMMe%2BBqkzlf%0AwEcilliLec8uMyQQrqzEaFcd5WRTyrdbUQ%3D%3D%0A/e61503baf9fe450f)

body:
The Founders didn't defeat one tyranny to hand us another. Here's what we owe them.

| | | | | [|
---](https://ericburlisonforcongress.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b6500a115da3c4344522b1e48&id=0fd775684a&e=5f9dc01b8c)
| | Peter ,
Two hundred and fifty years ago, ordinary Americans did something extraordinary. Farmers, blacksmiths, and shopkeepers picked up muskets and stood against the most powerful empire on earth. They pledged their lives, their fortunes, and their sacred honor, and many of them paid in full.
They did it for one reason. Freedom.
They did not defeat one tyranny just to build another, one that buries our kids in debt, tries to control your medicine, register your firearms, and tell you what you can put on your own dinner table. That is not the country they built. They gave us a limited government, and it is our job to keep it that way.
[](https://ericburlisonforcongress.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=b6500a115da3c4344522b1e48&id=7c7e9f2de9&e=5f9dc01b8c)
But here's the truth: freedom is never more than one generation from being lost. The bureaucrats in Washington are not going to limit themselves. It falls to us, the people who still believe in the Founders' vision, to defend it.
That is exactly what I am fighting for in Congress. Standing up for the Second Amendment. Getting Washington out from between you and your doctor. Getting bureaucrats off the backs of our Missouri farmers. And reining in the reckless spending that threatens our children's future.
I can't do it without you. If you believe America deserves another 250 years of freedom, will you chip in today to help us keep up the fight?

Farmers, blacksmiths, and shopkeepers picked up muskets and stood against the most powerful empire on earth. They pledged their lives, their fortunes, and their sacred honor, and many of them paid in full. They did it for one reason. Freedom. They did not defeat one tyranny just to build another, one that buries our kids in debt, tries to control your medicine, register your firearms, and tell you what you can put on your own dinner table. That is not the country they built. They gave us a limited government, and it is our job to keep it that way. But here's the truth: freedom is never more than one generation from being lost. The bureaucrats in Washington are not going to limit themselves. It falls to us, the people who still believe in the Founders' vision, to defend it. That is exactly what I am fighting for in Congress. Standing up for the Second Amendment. Getting Washington out from between you and your doctor. alongside unregulated crypto to amass a jaw-dropping fortune. And now,

passing the Clarity Act, a dangerous new regulatory framework for digital
currencies...written by crypto lobbyists themselves.

Now those same lobbyists are RACING to get this bill across the finish
line before the August recess – and together we’re going to stop it.

But the only way to stop the Clarity Act is by flooding Congress with

The bottom line is that when families can't make ends meet, they are forced to make serious choices. They delay medical care; stop buying healthy food in favor of cheaper, more heavily processed options; and even skip meals altogether. Ultimately, they often go further into debt. As bad as that is, the more challenging part for families near or below the poverty line is figuring out how to get out of that hole in an era of stagnating incomes, declining upward mobility, and rising costs of everyday necessities.
When asked what he would say to the 60% of Americans who live paycheck to paycheck, Rep. Troy Nehls (R-TX) said "maybe the 60% of Americans don't work as hard as I do..."
Mike Rogers has shown the same concern about the affordability crisis as he does about every issue his constituents face: he hasn't said a word about it...

[The Problem With Low Wage Companies](https://swo5c8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001duZXLQYB3LfCTBxgGUQJpCAreyZRc-MdcX_2V9eiyxWAGWMy9mH-TbtoF2JCwWZi4cklr4RVIbzVWLjgcyARM7XHmz0sl4wvw8BdoCFZDurZMKT2WBpPDU_t3O6AlqY2cKDfLwjVbd_a1EkzRaEuQp8C71jycqacfmiQuY-FBeQ5n5cWf2UDcA6e0TlT8YqokgnqSbQ33gTye5dvVP6SEQ==&c=NFoxPWaNELOQ_VdLN7rZciA5rb_a6Qo4vGNXZB0XxLoHAyBWbVim4w==&ch=d_vck7Qfp_9yTJaCQZbeOctaosyQ0Juk6eZB8_R_3M-mpMVb1XkWBw==)
---
In March of this year, the Institute for Policy Studies (IPS) released a report on a group of companies it referred to as the "Low Wage 20." The report examines the 20 publicly held corporations in the S&P 500 that are the largest employers of low-wage workers. It included facts like these:

* 15 of the Low-Wage 20 reported median pay in 2024 below the $35,631 income limit for a family of three to be eligible for Medicaid in most states.
* 13 of the 20 reported median pay below the $33,576 threshold for a family of three to be eligible for SNAP food aid in 2024.
* Walmart alone likely has around 468,800 employees on Medicaid.

For contrast, the average CEO salary for these companies is $18.9 billion, or 899 times the median salary of their employees.

# One Last Thought Until Next Week
---
| | |
---
I hope everyone had a great 4th of July. It's important to remember that while we celebrate the beginning of this experiment in democracy, we also recognize that it has not ended.
We got to visit with people in LaFayette, Heflin, and Jacksonville as they celebrated the 250th anniversary of this nation's birth. All of them were excited about the holiday, and many were eager to meet someone running to represent them. What they wanted to talk about wasn't surprising. They're worried about the cost of living. They worry about the lack of health care in their area. They're worried about the care they will receive for the injuries they suffered in service to our nation. They don't think their government cares about them.
We won't fix those problems overnight, but if we commit to continuing the American Revolution this November at the ballot box, we know things will get better.
Those in and around St. Clair County and Pell City, don't forget we have a town hall meeting on July 9. Details are on the calendar. All our town halls are open to the public, and we don't pre-screen questions.
We're 119 days away from the general election.

We'll talk soon,

Lee

### _What does it mean to love our country?_
It's certainly not a new question, but one I've been thinking about as we prepared to commemorate the 250th anniversary of our nation's founding.
Americans have much to be proud of - and much that brings us shame. Acknowledging that latter part makes some people very angry.
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/c7a8394b-ff29-47ba-8c68-0991bbcf4b35?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
More than 40 volunteers marched on July 4th weekend, despite the heat and storms, to celebrate our nation's founding.
Readying to launch into the Farragut 4th of July Parade route early Saturday morning, I told our volunteer cavalry that **it is an act of patriotism to not only want better for our country, but to show up and work for it.**
This parade felt different than many others we've done. While plenty of folks were excited to see us, many more were subdued. I saw one man telling his children, whose shirts were plastered with "Marsha Marsha Marsha" stickers, not to wave at us. Even as we smiled, wished them a happy Fourth, and gave them candy.
Another man about my age, upon locking eyes with me, gave me an aggressive thumbs down and shouted out across the asphalt, "You hate America."
I wasn't surprised.
That's what Donald Trump says about people like me, who have the audacity to disagree with his vision for our country's future. It's a line frequently parroted by Tim Burchett when he's on camera.
It's a line repeated on right-wing media stations intended to divide and dehumanize. To make us see each other as enemies, not as neighbors -- as people who also love our country and want the best for it, even if we may disagree on what it looks like and how we get there.
When Donald Trump or Tim Burchett says it, I see it for what it is: a tool intended to sow division and discord. When my East Tennessee neighbor says it, I'm saddened it has been deployed so effectively.
**Because, unsurprisingly, I do love my country. I wouldn 't be running for office, working 60+ hour weeks, giving up a year with my business and precious time with my loved ones if I didn't love our nation.**
Even though time is scarce on the campaign trail, I've been slowly making my way through the book _These Truths: A History of the United States_ by Jill Lepore. And **it has reminded me that it 's just about the most American thing to disagree - loudly - about the future of our country.**
Our beloved and revered Constitution (that our elected officials and service members vow to uphold, of which I keep a copy of in my bag) barely scraped through tumultuous months of debate and razor-thin ratification margins in the states.
Our framers couldn't agree on how democratic to make this new government. How to apportion representation. How to deal with the horrific institution of slavery. They made decisions and enshrined values that we later disagreed with, and _changed._
The constitutional republic created by the framers included representation only for white men. **The reason that anyone else is included in this governance for and by the people is because our ancestors saw that this experiment was unfinished, and they fought for something new and something better.**
I know the moment we are in feels unprecedented. But the process of working towards a more perfect union, and fighting for who all is to be included in this experiment in democracy - and what we believe the role of government to be - is something that every generation of Americans has done. Not something every American has done, mind you. Every _generation_ of Americans. Some people sit these decisions out, giving more weight and voice to those who do step up and speak out.
Governance of, for, and by the people will never be easy. It will never come without debate and deliberation and effort. It's up to us to ask what we hope for the present and the future, and work to make it so. As a reminder, [here's what I hope for and am working so tirelessly towards](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/8f942cb5-f106-4caf-8829-1e0884f48348?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). If you share my vision, won't you [join me](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/a6b4dbc7-d2b1-4071-bda6-5b2d942206e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in working towards it?
Today is the deadline to [register to vote](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/7b29c429-7871-4296-b74d-486c54e7a24c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for the August 6th election, in which we will elect local officials and vote in the state and federal primaries.
**May you be driven by love of our country and your fellow Americans to take up the mantle of our democracy.**
_Because now it is our turn._
Michaela

body:
| Peter,

When special interests and party bosses inject money into Mariannette Miller-Meeks' campaign, they're not doing it because they want what's best for our district. | Peter—

Banning abortion and putting women’s health and lives at risk isn’t enough for anti-abortion extremists.

[Now, anti-abortion politicians want to punish women who get abortions by throwing them in jail.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/134801412/632210587/-2116918780?sourceid=1151439&utm_campaign=26emige-0618aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=fightback&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkMmU3OTdlMC0xMDdhLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=RFsdd8Wx8LnkV6c5udhx-igUGD-wxLsyQ4IckP7eecc=&emci=8cd1b08c-1e70-f111-ac9c-000d3a54bed0&emdi=d2e797e0-107a-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ceid=954237)

Prominent anti-abortion leaders and politicians have called for states to remove legal protections for women who get abortions—and Texas has answered the call, with lawmakers now debating repealing those protections and subjecting women who get abortions to criminal penalties.

**Too many people have already had to flee their states to seek abortion care after they were pushed to the brink of death.** [Extremists would seek to prosecute and punish these women for saving their own lives.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/134801415/632210590/-2116918780?sourceid=1151439&utm_campaign=26emige-0618aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=fightback&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkMmU3OTdlMC0xMDdhLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=RFsdd8Wx8LnkV6c5udhx-igUGD-wxLsyQ4IckP7eecc=&emci=8cd1b08c-1e70-f111-ac9c-000d3a54bed0&emdi=d2e797e0-107a-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ceid=954237)

We cannot allow this dangerous rhetoric to move forward. We must show that the public rejects this dangerous agenda.

[Sign the petition now and send a clear message: pregnant people should never be treated like criminals for making decisions about their own bodies or their health.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/134801416/632210591/-2116918780?sourceid=1151439&utm_campaign=26emige-0618aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=fightback&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkMmU3OTdlMC0xMDdhLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=RFsdd8Wx8LnkV6c5udhx-igUGD-wxLsyQ4IckP7eecc=&emci=8cd1b08c-1e70-f111-ac9c-000d3a54bed0&emdi=d2e797e0-107a-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ceid=954237)

In solidarity,

Center for Reproductive Rights

The _New York Times_ sat on the ugliest reporting about Graham Platner and gave the public a watered-down substitute, according to the paper's own source for the June 4th story that first publicized the Democrat nominee's abusive behavior toward multiple women.
Lyndsey Fifield, the ex-girlfriend of Platner's who was named by the _Times_ , detailed Tuesday how alleged journalists for the paper obtained reams of evidence from her, including a full rolodex of potential witnesses -- most of whom they didn't even bother to call.
Fifield had previously alleged that the _Times_ coaxed her to come forward by name by assuring her that other women were also coming forward by name.
That ended up being a lie.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..KNdbKVUiRrorcL3lB2JnZmbF0b2VBTq9Yw3Y9H6hRPE?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=205773657)
Instead, the _Times_ ignored what Fifield described in a Tuesday statement as the most serious evidence and the best supporting sources that she provided to them. They positioned Fifield, a Republican staffer in Washington, D.C., as the leading accuser and cast her allegations as political suspicious. The barely concealed subtext of the story was that a Republican woman could not be believed when making an allegation of sexual misconduct. The resulting story systematically downplayed and failed to corroborate credible allegations of abuse against Maine Democratic Senate nominee.
Fifield, who dated Platner from around 2013 to 2015, poured out the details in a lengthy X thread on Tuesday.
She provided the _Times_ with contact information for five friends who could affirm the timeline and her accounts of abuse, screenshots of messages with roommates about Platner stalking her row house (just five houses down from his), emails to her landlord urgently breaking her lease to flee across town, diary entries with timestamps, and more. Reporters spoke only to two friends she explicitly noted wouldn't know the abuse details but could verify context. They ignored the others. They declined to contact her ex-fiance or priest from pre-marital counseling, where she had disclosed the terror triggered by his temper. Despite this mountain of contemporaneous evidence, the paper's most-shared line claimed they "could not corroborate" her story.'
The _Times_ story could have started: "Multiple women have come forward to accuse Democratic Senate nominee Graham Platner of domestic violence, according to a New York _Times_ investigation..."
**Instead, the supposed journalists began their political spin with the following paragraph:**
> "On Tuesday evening, after a whirlwind day in Washington, Graham Platner, the Democratic candidate for Senate in Maine, rushed home. Rumors were spreading from Portland to the Potomac about Mr. Platner's messy personal life, [after news reports](https://substack.com/redirect/28b5b10a-d689-433c-ac9b-66fee5b09b5e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that he had sent sexual messages to women while married. Democratic senators were pressing him about whether more damaging revelations were coming. Journalists were swarming, staking out his hometown. Amid the turmoil, Mr. Platner worked the phones, rolling through calls to ex-girlfriends who might publicly acknowledge that while he may have been a bad boyfriend, he was, in fact, a decent guy."
**Now, compare that to what Fifield said Tuesday about her attempts to provide corroborating information to reporters Lisa Lerer and Katie Glueck.**
> I actually understand why Democrat leaders didn't take our stories seriously when the Times reported them in June but are taking them seriously now.
>
> It was by design.
>
> The line most shared from the piece was the claim that the Times "could not corroborate" my story despite talking to two of my friends.
>
> I gave them the contact information for five friends.
>
> They called the two who I clarified would not know about the abuse but would be able to affirm our relationship timeline, events, etc.
>
> They simply did not call the other three.
>
> I also gave them the names of all my former roommates who remembered him stalking our row house (which was about 5 houses down from his) and waiting for me to return. I gave them screenshots of messages between these roommates and I discussing it.
>
> I gave them the names of other men I dated who might have remembered him following us around the hill and showing up on my stoop after we walked home from dates to confront us. I gave them emails to my landlord urgently ending my lease and moving to an apartment across town and diary entries talking about it - all time marked.
>
> I told them that during pre-marital counseling I had spoken to my ex-fiance about the abuse because I had to explain to him why I reacted with such terror any time he lost his temper. They said oh NO we don't need to bother HIM (or my priest). Besides, I had written about it in my diary in detail, they reassured.
>
> As the weeks dragged on I stopped trying to give them evidence because the amount I had already given them seemed to overwhelm them and I thought it meant they clearly had more than enough to verify my every claim.
>
> My friends might not have known the details of the abuse, but they affirmed that yes, I had told them that he was abusive--long before he ran for Senate.
>
> Besides, they assured, my part in their reporting would be small. I thought my details would only serve to affirm Jenny and the other anonymous woman.
>
> Jenny and I - having never met or spoken - both shared with these reporters terrifyingly similar details of intimate partner violence, coercive control, and cycles of abuse/love bombing. The third unnamed woman in the story did as well.
>
> But tell me again how they "could not corroborate."

## The story the Times chose not to tell
Racicot was in that June story too -- as a footnote. She told the _Times_ only that Platner's behavior was "reckless" and "unsettling," that he'd shown up at her house drunk after she asked him not to. Mild stuff, the way it ran.
On Sunday she told Politico the rest of it. She said that on a night in late 2021, Platner let himself into her unlocked rural Maine home, nearly blackout drunk, after she'd told him not to come, and forced her to have sex while she repeatedly told him to stop.
Platner calls the accusation "categorically untrue" and says any claim of non-consensual behavior is false, but the dam has broken.
Ruben Gallego rescinded. Adam Schiff called the allegations deeply troubling and urged Platner to end his campaign. Chuck Schumer and Kirsten Gillibrand demanded he withdraw immediately so Maine Democrats can pick someone who can beat Susan Collins. John Fetterman went after the backers who stood by him.
Platner, for his part, denies everything and says he's "taking the time to reflect on the best path forward."
Perhaps the _Times_ and its subscribers should also do some reflecting.

name: Power the Polls
subject: Real people, real impact – will you sign up?
body:
You’re getting this message from [ https://act.powerthepolls.org/go/4508?t=1001&akid=9056%2E934366%2EskOfGB ]Power the Polls because you signed up
to learn about serving as a poll worker. If you no longer wish to hear
from us, [ https://act.powerthepolls.org/cms/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?akid=9056.934366.skOfGB&t=1002&akid=9056%2E934366%2EskOfGB ]please unsubscribe here. Marking emails as spam can affect our
ability to reach others with important information.

[ https://act.powerthepolls.org/go/42?t=1003&akid=9056%2E934366%2EskOfGB ][IMG]

Hey Peter—

The sunburns are fading, and the BBQs are taking a break – but there’s
still time to commemorate America 250.

[ https://act.powerthepolls.org/go/4922?t=1004&akid=9056%2E934366%2EskOfGB ]At Power the Polls that means serving your community by recruiting as
many poll workers as possible before elections kick off across the country
in the fall.

Poll workers are the unsung heroes of democracy, they literally keep
elections running smoothly, and we couldn’t vote without them. Don’t take
it from us, hear what these poll workers had to say about their
experience:

“It was one of the most gratifying experiences that I have ever had.
Walking in, and seeing so many different people from different walks of
life, walking in and out, and helping them do their civic duty to
society. It was so gratifying to help people do this.” - Abhi

“[Poll workers are] politically diverse, and in every other way, just
being able to come together. To me, it was just this feeling of, Wow,
this is like, this is America, like at its best. And that was really
energizing.” - Josh

“And I just really enjoy being in my community and helping empower the
people in my community to use their voice. Working the polls is like
helping people vote, and it's really empowering nonpartisan work. So I
really like appreciate working in my community and seeing familiar faces
at my precinct, because I've worked at the same precinct for years now.
“ - Mallory

We’re looking for more folks like Abhi, Josh, and Mallory to step up and
serve their community – that could be you!

Get started on your application, we’re here to answer any questions along
the way:

[ https://act.powerthepolls.org/go/4888?t=1005&akid=9056%2E934366%2EskOfGB ]Apply Now

Thanks,

—Power the Polls Team

You can unsubscribe from this mailing list at any time:

You don't get your bills passed in this state if leadership doesn't want you to...

Every bill any of us brought on illegal immigration this session. Dead. Even our simple bill to audit the NGOs bringing migrants here. I just wanted an audit. Where's the money going? Who's getting moved where? Who's checking any of it?

Never got a hearing either. Not voted down, nobody had to put their name on it, it just never showed up on a calendar. You want to know how a state kills a bill without anyone answering for it? That's how.

Let's check on DC real quick:

**> > HR 9535 **sits in Congress right now. Amnesty for anyone who worked, _or says they worked_ in ag (Idaho congressman and maybe one of the biggest clowns in DC, Mike Simpson is a cosponsor)

**> > H-2A** goes from seasonal to year round too, so American workers get priced out of whole industries while nobody's watching

Last year some Idaho state legislators flew to the White House and got told to do something about illegal immigration. _Then they came home and did nothing._ But some of those same guys had zero problem flying to Mar-a-Lago to help push Trump's family crypto investments (and even missed votes during our own legislative session doing it).

Same people. Not a coincidence, not two separate groups doing two separate things. One trip mattered enough to skip work for. The other one they came home from empty handed.

That's the uniparty for you.

I've been in office a few years now and that's basically the whole lesson. State level, national level, it's one circus with different clowns rotating through.

Case in point, the Epstein stuff. Idaho house reps Simpson and Fulcher voted to send H.Res. 1100 back to committee instead of letting it get a direct vote. That's the resolution that would've forced the House Ethics Committee to actually release its sexual harassment and abuse investigation records. Send it back to committee and you never have to vote against transparency on the record (neat trick).

But I digress...

Because in a few weeks another batch of Idaho Republicans get flown to the White House for head pats.

Want to bet how that goes?

**Americans get screwed. That's how it goes.**

Trump's people are floating dairy visas that work like amnesty. So we lock down the border with one hand and wave people through the back door with the other. Cool system.

And I still can't tell you exactly where NGO money's landing in Idaho. That's the whole point of the bill I couldn't get a hearing on. But I can tell you the one bill that would've answered that question got squashed before anyone had to vote against it.

"Vote them out!!!"

I hear it constantly.

_Nope. You guys keep voting for the same clowns year after year._

Turnout in Idaho sits in the low 20s. So that door's not open right now. And even when it is open, basically nobody walks through it.

Precinct committeeman seats though? Tons of them sit empty because nobody bothers filing. _This is the actual foundation the party sits on._ And county central committee fills those vacant seats with whoever they want, with no primary needed. Whoever holds one votes on who the party backs next cycle.

So call your county clerk.

Ask who holds yours. If it's vacant, there's your in.

_**Put your trust in God. Build real relationships with the people around you, your family, your neighbors, your friends. Take care of your own house and people and sphere of influence best you can.**_

Because most of these guys give zero shits about you.

subject: Sign on to stop these voter registration raids
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Integrity First Voter Action Project, www
body:

It's clear that MAGA's endgame is a country where only their supporters vote. They don't want new people in the democratic process, and they question every ballot cast by someone that doesn't look or think like them.
Now, Trump and the sycophants he's appointed are trying to use the power and authority of the federal government to make their suppressive dreams a reality. We all must stand up to stop them.
Please, Team, send your letter to Congress and hold our leaders accountable for this raid, ensuring they protect voter registration groups and others defending our fundamental right to vote >> [https://actionnetwork.org/letters/dont-let-the-fbi-attack-voter-registration-drives/?source=direct_link&referrer=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&redirect=https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-actions]
START WRITING NOW ⇨ [https://actionnetwork.org/letters/dont-let-the-fbi-attack-voter-registration-drives/?source=direct_link&referrer=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&redirect=https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-actions]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
Trump and his allies were already purging voters, restricting the ballot, and lying about election results, Team. Now the FBI has gone even further, with a raid on organizers and volunteers registering their neighbors to vote.
Federal agents just raided the Cleveland office of the Ohio Organizing Collaborative, a group known for voter registration and community organizing, and reportedly seized documents and computer files. They’ve denied the public information about why the group was targeted, what justified the raid, or whether political pressure played any role.
The right to vote is sacred. At a time when extremists are working overtime to kick eligible voters off the rolls, shut people out of the ballot box, and attack the organizers who help communities fight back, Congress must demand answers now.
Demand Congress investigate the FBI raid on the Ohio Organizing Collaborative, protect voter registration groups from political intimidation, and defend our right to vote >> [https://actionnetwork.org/letters/dont-let-the-fbi-attack-voter-registration-drives/?source=direct_link&referrer=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&redirect=https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-actions]
START WRITING NOW ⇨ [https://actionnetwork.org/letters/dont-let-the-fbi-attack-voter-registration-drives/?source=direct_link&referrer=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&redirect=https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-actions]
The goal of this raid was simple and dangerous: To intimidate all of us and to make voting harder for the people most likely to be ignored, excluded, or suppressed.
Voter registration drives are a lifeline for voters of color, low-income voters, young voters, immigrant communities, and people who already face barriers at the ballot box. When those drives are threatened, eligible voters are silenced before they ever get to cast a ballot.
Already, Trump and his allies have purged the voter rolls, restricted access, harassed organizers, criminalized assistance, and cast suspicion on the people helping communities participate in democracy. Congress must finally take decisive action to defend our freedom to vote.
Send your letter to ask Congress to investigate this raid, expose the truth, and protect voter registration groups before another raid does lasting damage >> [https://actionnetwork.org/letters/dont-let-the-fbi-attack-voter-registration-drives/?source=direct_link&referrer=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&redirect=https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-actions]

Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country.
Since the Supreme Court gutted key provisions in the Voting Rights Act, extreme politicians have taken advantage to pass harsh laws that restrict access to the ballot box. These restrictions particularly affect disadvantaged communities and people of color. It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities.
Your support is crucial to our efforts. Will you donate today to help us protect voting rights? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/integrity-first-voter-action-project-1?refcode=070726_1&amount=20]

From parade routes to the PFD, here's what drove Hughes/Gettys this week.

| | | | |
---
| | Happy 250th Birthday USA!
---
**Greetings, Alaskans: ** **There's something telling about a campaign that shows up not just at fundraisers, but in parade lines alongside neighbors, waving flags on America's 250th birthday. Hughes/Gettys volunteers turned out across the state this Fourth of July weekend, and the energy in those crews reflects why this ticket has earned its reputation as the people's choice.**
**Being the people's choice means being straight with Alaskans, even when it's easier not to be. On the PFD, I'm not making promises I can't keep. I'm committed to introducing a full statutory PFD and fighting for the largest divided the legislature will pass, while tackling the root causes that have made that fight so hard: unsustainable spending and a private sector that hasn't been given room to grow. Alaskans also deserve a governor who will fight to put Alaska lands in Alaska hands and finally build the infrastructure this state has been shortchanged on for too long.**
**Blake and I are in this together, and so is this growing coalition of Alaskans who are ready for leadership that delivers results instead of slogans. Scroll down for parade photos, a fundraiser recap, and a conversation worth joining.**
**Please know not only does your support mean the world to us, but the very message that resonates with you, needs to get out across our huge state! I’m incredibly honored you’ve chosen to support our campaign. Together, we will rock this race! Every dollar moves us closer to the finish line. We’re not ashamed to say it: we need you! name: Hannah Servedio
subject: Our volunteers make all the difference. So does pizza.
body:
https://va4reprofreedom.org/ [https://va4reprofreedom.org/]
https://va4reprofreedom.org/get-involved/ [https://va4reprofreedom.org/get-involved/]
Hi Friend,
Summer is heating up, and so is our campaign.
Our team is preparing to launch a canvass program that will reach every corner of the Commonwealth. Later this summer we’ll be knocking on doors to share what’s at stake on November 3: abortion, birth control, maternal healthcare, and more.
We need our neighbors to vote a resounding “YES” and enshrine reproductive freedom in Virginia’s Constitution this fall.
To get ready, we’re inviting supporters to attend volunteer trainings in Richmond [https://secure.ngpvan.com/s3913lc5wk--6WiZpZ92KA2] , Arlington [https://secure.ngpvan.com/u1AEHiIdfk6-jsGlmXQ0Uw2] , Charlottesville [https://secure.ngpvan.com/WweChtpVRUebZaL7kWZegA2] , and Virginia Beach [https://secure.ngpvan.com/oRcpWnTYh0qsxCKogSCo4Q2] the weekend of July 18 & 19. Will you become an activist in your community?
YES, I'LL SIGN UP! [https://va4reprofreedom.org/get-involved/]
Volunteer sign-ups are already outpacing what we’d expected. We are thrilled to see so many people join our movement and give their time to the cause.
But we have a problem: a pizza budget gap problem. The least we can do is provide our volunteers with a slice to eat... but we need some help.
Friend, if you’re not able to attend our training, please chip in a few bucks to help feed our volunteers: [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/vaforrepro-em?refcode=070726]
$5 = 2 slices of pizza [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/vaforrepro-em?refcode=070726]
$10 = 4 slices of pizza [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/vaforrepro-em?refcode=070726]
$25 = 10 slices of pizza [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/vaforrepro-em?refcode=070726]
Want to give another amount? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/vaforrepro-em?refcode=070726]
Whether you join in person, help provide lunch to our volunteers, or both, your support will help us build our grassroots movement that will carry us to victory on November 3.
In gratitude,
Hannah Servedio
Organizing Director
P.S. Join us on July 18 or 19 for training , [https://va4reprofreedom.org/get-involved/] bring a friend, and knock on doors in your community this summer. Or, chip in to fuel the team: [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/vaforrepro-em?refcode=070726] it all makes a difference on our way to victory this November.
Visit our website [https://va4reprofreedom.org/]
Virginians for Reproductive Freedom
600 Pennsylvania Ave SE Unit 15845
Washington, DC 20003

**Seniors deserve to age at home without scams draining Medicare dollars **_America’s aging population will make home-based care increasingly important in the years ahead_ By Bobby Jindal & Newt Gingrich
---
One of the most important transformations in American healthcare is taking place outside hospitals and nursing homes. Advances in artificial intelligence, telehealth, remote monitoring, home health services, and new care delivery models are making it possible for more Americans to receive high-quality care in the place they most want to be: their own homes. For seniors, this transformation represents an extraordinary opportunity. Most older Americans want to remain in their homes, maintaining their independence and connection to family and community. Aging in place is not simply a personal preference. It is a matter of dignity and quality of life. President Donald Trump recognized this reality when he pledged to help seniors remain in their homes longer. Since returning to office, his administration has taken meaningful steps toward this goal. Earlier this year, President Trump signed legislation extending Medicare's Acute Hospital Care at Home program through 2030, allowing eligible seniors to receive hospital-level care without leaving their homes. His administration has continued implementation of the GUIDE dementia model, helping patients with Alzheimer's disease and related conditions remain at home longer while supporting family caregivers. It has also preserved Medicare telehealth flexibilities that allow more care to be delivered directly to patients rather than requiring unnecessary trips to hospitals and clinics. President Donald Trump recognized this reality when he pledged to help seniors remain in their homes longer. Since returning to office, his administration has taken meaningful steps toward this goal. Earlier this year, President Trump signed legislation extending Medicare's Acute Hospital Care at Home program through 2030, allowing eligible seniors to receive hospital-level care without leaving their homes. His administration has continued implementation of the GUIDE dementia model, helping patients with Alzheimer's disease and related conditions remain at home longer while supporting family caregivers. It has also preserved Medicare telehealth flexibilities that allow more care to be delivered directly to patients rather than requiring unnecessary trips to hospitals and clinics. | | Email sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com by AmericaNext

subject: A special weekend with my neighbors
body:
|

Peter, There is no place like home. Getting away from the extremism in Washington and coming home always seems to clarify that, behind the noise, there are real people who just want to get to know each other and rally around each other’s challenges. To know that, behind the loudest headlines, we ultimately all want the same things, like for working families to live in safe neighborhoods with reliable infrastructure, affordable goods, and quality jobs. **That made this past weekend extra special, as our communities celebrated our 250th anniversary as a young nation, one that has had ups and downs but never lost sight of what it means to make sure our neighbors are well-fed and taken care of.** It was even better that I had the privilege to celebrate in multiple festivities across the district. Whether it was taking part in the Quad Cities' oldest 4th of July Parade, right in the heart of Morgan Park:
Or celebrating the nation's birthday in East Moline with so many neighbors -- and rocking a “George says 7-6!” shirt (I _think_ the kids got a kick out of it):
It was another reminder that the most important work I do happens here at home, ensuring our district remains a beacon of hope, togetherness, and freedom. It means the world to me to be a trusted neighbor in IL-17, across communities large and small. And I remain steadfast in my commitment to be the best representative and the best person I can be -- for my neighbors, for our region, and for our country. I hope you had a special holiday with your neighbors, and I wish you all the best as we move through July. -Eric | [Donate](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/134809137/632232182/-1060083271?refcode=em-7.7.26-all-a&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS85MzkwNSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4NDJhMzRjMy0xOTdhLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=EIGQQzGxn-1BnVh_2NrZKhEK-B3rNxMpSEgCpklW0yI=)
