name: Sue Anderbois
subject: Ward 3 PVD News
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Friends of AnderBois
body:
| |
---
Hello Friends & Neighbors,

Summer is in full swing! It’s so lovely to bump into you all at the farmers market or walking on Camp or Hope or Benefit Street!

I have been keeping busy for you all on Council — so lots of updates below! We will also be having our July Ward 3 meeting on July 29th (location still being solidified) — I’ll post final information on location via social media and in an email prior to the meeting!

And as a reminder — the Council goes on its one-month recess for August. There will be no Council meetings/committees, etc at City Hall during that time. But I am, as always, available via email or phone.

|
| **Neighborhood Update and Upcoming Events** There are lots of things happening in the ward — and meetings happening at City Hall!
**New Sidewalks:** The Department of Public Works will continue their investment in new sidewalks in high-traffic areas later this summer with new sidewalks along Hope Street near Lippitt Park. This will also include the section of 9th St off of Hope that has been a tripping hazard for some time.
**Active Construction:** The utilities will be doing some active work under several roads in our ward throughout the summer. This will include Cypress Street (North Main to Knowles) and Locust Street. Both should be wrapped up by the end of July.
**Nathan Bishop Courts:** The Nathan Bishop Courts are currently being painted and should be open very soon! The painters needed a few solid days without any precipitation and without major humidity so that the paint could dry appropriately — and we are almost there! Councilwoman Davidson and I will plan a ribbon-cutting celebration with the community for later this month to celebrate the new courts. Thank you to everyone who has provided feedback — I know you all are eagerly awaiting the ability to play on the courts (as am I!).
**Full City Council Meeting:** The Full City Council Meeting will be at 6pm on July 16th. This will be our last full meeting before the Council’s August recess, though committees can continue to meet until July 31. As always, the Council will reconvene in September.
**Reading of the Declaration of Independence:** Join us for the reading of the Declaration of Independence on July 8th, 5:30pm at North Burial Ground! The Sons of the American Revolution will meet at the Rochambeau Gate and then walk to Stephen Hopkins' grave to read and reflect on the signing of the Declaration of Independence.
**SOULstice Summer Music Series:** The Mount Hope Community Center is hosting the SOULstice Summer Music Series on July 18th, 5:00pm-6:30pm at Billy Taylor Park.
**Swell Folk Fest in Lippitt Park:** The day after PVD Fest, September 20th, Ward 3’s Lippitt Park will be host to the Swell Folk Festival — an all-day music festival!

---

**Miscellaneous Topics For You** There are several important topics being discussed in Council now, or that affect Ward 3, that I wanted to share:
**FY27 Budget:** The Council passed the amended FY27 budget, which was signed by the Mayor in June. The budget keeps tax rates level. The Council also prioritized investments in several areas of particular importance to me and Ward 3 residents, which includes: additional funding for the libraries and rec centers; additional staffing for emergency management and in the City’s Sustainability Department to help implement our clean energy and energy-savings programs; new staff at DPW to ensure implementation of my ordinance that holds the utilities accountable for doing quality work and not leaving our roads a mess after construction; investments to support our veterans.
**PPSD Return to Local Control:** The schools returned to local control as of July 1. PPSD has long cited the City’s procurement process as a barrier to effectively and efficiently keeping our schools stocked with necessary supplies. I want to commend Ward 2 Councilwoman Davidson for convening a working group and introducing legislation (that I have cosponsored) to improve the process PPSD uses for procurement while maintaining proper oversight over taxpayer dollars. This ordinance will have its second passage on July 16th, and hopefully be signed into law by the Mayor.
**Juvenile Hearing Board:** I was so proud to vote to support updates to the City’s Juvenile Hearing Board process. This updated ordinance helps ensure kids who are eligible to be diverted through the JHB process — instead of going through the criminal justice system — have that opportunity. One small mistake should not ruin a child’s life, and this ordinance ensures that more kids are given a second chance and the support they need to learn from their mistakes.
**“8-law” Amendments:** There is a law referred to as “8-law” meant to help the development and operation of affordable housing units. For the last several years, developers have been able to utilize it for subsidizing buildings that are primarily market-rate housing. The Council has passed legislation that helps close this loophole to ensure that incentives for affordable housing are only used for affordable housing. This legislation still needs to pass for a second time on July 16 and then will hopefully be signed into law by the mayor. (If there is a veto, we would need to reconvene during recess for the 2⁄3 majority required to override a veto.)
**North Main Street:** There continues to be a lot of progress on our ongoing work on North Main! Our next newsletter will focus on these updates — but a teaser is that the City is in the process of contracting with a firm for the design/engineering process for larger structural changes for the roadway; there are 3 projects in the works to develop underutilized plots of land, and we are working with RIDOT and the Streets Coalition on another intersection safety improvement involving planters and beautification. Stay tuned for more!

---

**Follow My Socials For Live Updates!** In between newsletters, I try to keep active on social media! Follow me on Instagram, Bluesky, and Facebook for more regular updates! You can also always reach me via email at **AnderBois.Ward3@gmail.com**. | [](https://sue4ri.com/l/gAcx0nYPfyiC) | [](https://sue4ri.com/l/If7wA5uIM4j2) | [](https://sue4ri.com/l/56fwfKoGpBcC)
---|---|---

It continues to be the honor of my life to serve as your City Councilor! Thank you for this opportunity to serve.

With Gratitude,

Sue A
---
|
* * *
**** This communications is on behalf of Sue AnderBois' City Council work ****

Councilor Sue AnderBois represents Ward 3, which includes the Mount Hope, Hope Village (Summit), Collyer Park, and Blackstone neighborhoods. She currently serves as the Deputy Majority Whip and the Chair of the North Main Street Task Force and the Special Committee on Environment and Resiliency. She is also a member of the Committee on Finance, Committee on City Property, Special Committee on Health, Opportunity, Prosperity, and Education (HOPE), and is a member of the Board of Parks Commissioners.

Her career has been focused on public policy solutions for climate change, clean energy, and sustainable food systems.
---
| Paid for by Friends of AnderBois
---

166 5th St, PVD 02906

# Samsung smashes 19x profit record but AI chip stocks still crater
Samsung Electronics **[posted a 19 fold surge in Q2 operating profit to about $58 billion dollars](https://substack.com/redirect/0382380a-2738-44f8-966b-e00481fab783?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** beating estimates yet shares slumped up to 10% in Seoul triggering declines across US chip makers and weighing on broader markets Tuesday.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3c9d0ae1-105d-42e7-9462-a731d60bf070?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Profit Taking Hits Hard:** Samsung shares which rose nearly 150% this year fell sharply despite results only 6% ahead of forecasts as investors worried about sustaining high AI related margins and spending plans.
* **Memory Bellwether Signals:** Samsung SK Hynix and Micron topped $1 trillion dollar valuation in May before pullback with high bandwidth memory shortages expected into 2027 yet results sparked broader semiconductor selloff.
* **US Indices Diverge:** S&P 500 slipped 0.1% and Nasdaq 0.5% while Dow rose modestly near record levels after Samsung news amid continued volatility in the tech trade.
* **Extreme Swings Hit Peers:** SK Hynix shares fell more than 6% and 17% this month adding uncertainty to its $28 billion dollar US listing though institutional interest reached up to $7 billion dollars.

# Musk's SpaceX blasts into Nasdaq 100 in just 15 explosive days
SpaceX **[entered the Nasdaq 100 index only 15 trading days](https://substack.com/redirect/3bb69ac6-6965-4ece-b1b5-258f45b2f8ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after shares began trading pulling the stock into major passive funds and potentially retirement accounts despite most shares remaining locked up with insiders.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a60c8869-047d-401e-b426-a7fb30240cc9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Passive Funds Must Buy:** Index trackers have to own Nasdaq 100 components forcing purchases of SpaceX and trims to other holdings to match benchmarks.
* **Supply Remains Tight:** Only a small slice of shares is publicly available with the rest held by insiders employees and early investors under lock up.
* **Nasdaq Rewrites Playbook:** The fast inclusion creates an unusual stock price setup at this scale for the world's largest IPO.
* **401k Exposure Looms:** Investors could soon see SpaceX stock appear in retirement portfolios through funds tied to the benchmark.

# Defense stocks explode as governments pour billions into weapons and AI
Defense stocks **[drove the iShares US Aerospace and Defense ETF](https://substack.com/redirect/a14855dd-73b9-4820-82e2-1cd9977fde11?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to a record high as rising military budgets weapons replenishment efforts and AI battlefield technology create demand for companies including RTX Boeing and Lockheed Martin.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5074cfc3-0041-48f9-9b92-c18f25ba363e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Budget Request Explodes:** Fiscal year 2027 defense spending ask hits $1.5 trillion dollars a 44% increase and the largest single year jump since World War II.
* **Contracts Flow Freely:** Lockheed Martin won a $35.3 billion dollar THAAD missile deal while RTX secured $400 million dollars for medium range air to air missiles.
* **Trump Meets Industry:** President Trump called in leaders from Lockheed Martin Boeing and Honeywell to ramp up production and rebuild depleted munitions stockpiles.
* **Tech Changes Demand:** Rapid innovation renders traditional systems obsolete spurring needs for advanced weapons cybersecurity space defenses and modern infrastructure.

# Nvidia Hesai lidar deal sparks serious US cyber security alarm
Hesai Technology **[a Shanghai based lidar maker blacklisted by the US Defense Department](https://substack.com/redirect/ba1146cd-697d-4582-85c9-8b2a27885fe4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** as a Chinese military entity partners with Nvidia to power autonomous vehicles and robots yet faces warnings it could enable data access or disruption.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/044e9ed7-8a77-489a-810d-95ab45d1c792?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Blacklist Does Not Ban:** Designation prevents Pentagon contracts but allows commercial use including in US robotaxis trucking and even airport security systems.
* **Nvidia Expansion Continues:** Hesai sensors integrate into Nvidia autonomous platforms as robotics becomes the chipmaker second biggest growth area after artificial intelligence.
* **Data Weaponization Risk:** Lidar point clouds create precise maps that experts say could be compromised by malware to target infrastructure or share with Beijing.
* **CEO Rejects Claims:** Hesai leader David Li denies military ties insists sensors hold no memory and calls the security narrative fiction while disclosing Chinese government oversight.

Nobody in American politics today is arguing that immigration is not a politically salient issue. Progressives like me argue that morally we can't throw immigrants under the bus and strategically we shouldn't cede the narrative ground to the far right, but we're not arguing that it doesn't have salience. This is despite the fact that essentially nobody in America is being personally hurt by immigration. Indeed, in many of the places where immigration is most politically salient, almost nobody is personally interacting with immigrants at all--there aren't a whole lot of undocumented people or border-related disputes happening in, say, rural central Pennsylvania. But immigration still matters to people, because there's a political party and media ecosystem that rants about it constantly. Talking about an issue matters.
I mention this because I have written another piece, this one for _[Boston Review](https://substack.com/redirect/2b13e7f7-ed7f-4bbb-b785-c8f1a22c3ed0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ , arguing against "climate hushing"--the effort by a bunch of corporate- and billionaire-funded centrist think tanks to persuade Democrats to stop talking about climate change.
The piece attempts to methodically rebut each of the--often shockingly weak or dishonest--arguments made by the climate hushers about why climate change isn't a politically useful issue for Democrats (TL;DR: it totally is).
But in some ways that's almost besides the point. As we sweat through another deadly heat wave that has already [killed tens of thousands](https://substack.com/redirect/6f523361-0001-4678-a81e-307e7f99857a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in recent weeks, and contemplate that terrifying aphorism--this is both the hottest summer of our lives, and the coldest summer of the rest of our lives--it's worth insisting not only that there is electoral value in talking about climate, but also that there is a moral imperative to do so.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a4cad08a-aae5-444b-b1e2-b652ef468ddb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
As I write in the [piece](https://substack.com/redirect/2b13e7f7-ed7f-4bbb-b785-c8f1a22c3ed0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg):
> Though critics of climate activism like to position themselves as tellers of "[tough truths](https://substack.com/redirect/b6b58977-12cd-4a0f-bf91-e66625b69cf6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)," the toughest truth is that decarbonizing our economy can't be done obliquely. Whether or not Democrats talk about climate, you can bet that Leonard Leo, the Koch network, conservative media outlets, and the fossil fuel industry will keep working to lock us ever deeper into relying on oil and gas. In 2024 Fox News [ran more](https://substack.com/redirect/0ae4fa14-fbdb-47aa-b33b-f0552ac24ae9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) segments on climate change than CBS, ABC, NBC, PBS, and MSNBC combined; all that Democrats achieve by ceding the narrative on climate to the right is to guarantee that MAGA and Big Oil win the debate.
> This fact is so obvious that even some proponents of climate hushing, like Searchlight Senior Fellow Jane Flegal, acknowledge it. In [her words](https://substack.com/redirect/a65bd57a-2a3f-42c0-b9dd-e726fb6e1e7e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), "It is hard for me to imagine 'solving' climate change as a problem without somebody caring about climate change qua climate change." Flegal squares the circle with climate hushing by arguing it's a temporary measure--someday, maybe, things will look different, and we can talk about climate then. The problem is that physics doesn't care about politics: the more time we take, the greater the likelihood of truly [dystopian](https://substack.com/redirect/e2b42e63-0953-46fc-a72c-0a49359b3a89?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) scenarios. Plus, it's hard to imagine how a more favorable political context for climate talk could possibly arise without active efforts to build political will now. When white moderates complained in similar fashion about the civil rights movement, Martin Luther King criticized their "mythical concept of time" in _Why We Can 't Wait _(1964).
> We can't wait when it comes to climate change, either. In the end, this is about [whether](https://substack.com/redirect/365261bc-600e-4f30-bc04-aad02843bfbf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) we are able to maintain organized civilization on this planet. To push the line--now dominant across the corporatist wing of the Democratic Party--that we shouldn't discuss climate change is not only morally wrong; it carries water for the fossil fuel industry and the forces that got us here in the first place.
I hope you'll [read the rest of the piece](https://substack.com/redirect/2b13e7f7-ed7f-4bbb-b785-c8f1a22c3ed0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and--if you find it useful--[share it around](https://substack.com/redirect/99451b85-43c0-4f27-9613-08666df2f69b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). I think this is a message that we really need to be hammering home, especially as this summer of climate disasters continues.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4465bd42-d909-40ce-868d-78993386924e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

clean_body: Do we want to maintain human civilization on this planet or not? | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more Do we want to maintain human civilization on this planet or not? | | | Jul 7 | | | | | | | | | | | | Nobody in American politics today is arguing that immigration is not a politically salient issue. Progressives like me argue that morally we can't throw immigrants under the bus and strategically we shouldn't cede the narrative ground to the far right, but we're not arguing that it doesn't have salience. This is despite the fact that essentially nobody in America is being personally hurt by immigration. Indeed, in many of the places where immigration is most politically salient, almost nobody is personally interacting with immigrants at all--there aren't a whole lot of undocumented people or border-related disputes happening in, say, rural central Pennsylvania. But immigration still matters to people, because there's a political party and media ecosystem that rants about it constantly. Talking about an issue matters. I mention this because I have written another piece, this one for , arguing against "climate hushing"--the effort by a bunch of corporate- and billionaire-funded centrist think tanks to persuade Democrats to stop talking about climate change. The piece attempts to methodically rebut each of the--often shockingly weak or dishonest--arguments made by the climate hushers about why climate change isn't a politically useful issue for Democrats (TL;DR: it totally is). But in some ways that's almost besides the point. As we sweat through another deadly heat wave that has already in recent weeks, and contemplate that terrifying aphorism--this is both the hottest summer of our lives, and the coldest summer of the rest of our lives--it's worth insisting not only that there is electoral value in talking about climate, but also that there is a moral imperative to do so. | | ---|---|--- As I write in the : Though critics of climate activism like to position themselves as tellers of "," the toughest truth is that decarbonizing our economy can't be done obliquely. Whether or not Democrats talk about climate, you can bet that Leonard Leo, the Koch network, conservative media outlets, and the fossil fuel industry will keep working to lock us ever deeper into relying on oil and gas. In 2024 Fox News segments on climate change than CBS, ABC, NBC, PBS, and MSNBC combined; all that Democrats achieve by ceding the narrative on climate to the right is to guarantee that MAGA and Big Oil win the debate. This fact is so obvious that even some proponents of climate hushing, like Searchlight Senior Fellow Jane Flegal, acknowledge it. In , "It is hard for me to imagine 'solving' climate change as a problem without somebody caring about climate change qua climate change." Flegal squares the circle with climate hushing by arguing it's a temporary measure--someday, maybe, things will look different, and we can talk about climate then. The problem is that physics doesn't care about politics: the more time we take, the greater the likelihood of truly scenarios. Plus, it's hard to imagine how a more favorable political context for climate talk could possibly arise without active efforts to build political will now. When white moderates complained in similar fashion about the civil rights movement, Martin Luther King criticized their "mythical concept of time" in Why We Can 't Wait (1964). We can't wait when it comes to climate change, either. In the end, this is about we are able to maintain organized civilization on this planet. To push the line--now dominant across the corporatist wing of the Democratic Party--that we shouldn't discuss climate change is not only morally wrong; it carries water for the fossil fuel industry and the forces that got us here in the first place. I hope you'll , and--if you find it useful--. I think this is a message that we really need to be hammering home, especially as this summer of climate disasters continues. | | ---|---|--- P.S. I want to thank Ruth Rivera, Lisa Beade, and Charlie for signing up to support my work with a paid subscription. It really means a ton, thanks a million! Thanks for reading! At the GOP Senate debate, John Sununu told a roomful of Republicans he’s
running to send me back to “bussing tables” at my family’s “chicken
restaurant.” He meant it as an insult.

As if the people who work in restaurants — cooking your food, clearing
your plates, keeping family businesses alive — have something to be
embarrassed about.

My great-grandfather came to New Hampshire from Greece over a century ago
and opened a candy shop in Manchester. My family built it into a
restaurant that’s been serving our community ever since.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260707_1.A9ADK9&refcode=em20260707-1&t=1003&akid=7607%2E582294%2E9Zf0hP ]Puritan Backroom sign

John Sununu was born into a political dynasty. His father was governor and
White House Chief of Staff. His brother was governor. John went to
Washington and then spent the next 17 years cashing in with Big Oil, Big
Pharma, and Wall Street.

Oh, and his family business invested in a literal gold mine in Azerbaijan
that sells minerals to China. He’s never had to work hard a day in his
life — and his comments at that debate prove exactly what he thinks of
people who do.

The people who bus tables, flip burgers, and run small businesses in New
Hampshire don’t need a senator who looks down on them. They need one who
comes from them.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260707_1.A9ADK9&amount=5&refcode=em20260707-1&t=1022&akid=7607%2E582294%2E9Zf0hP ]Donate $5 »

John Sununu doesn’t know the real New Hampshire. I do. That’s why I’m
running for Senate.

— Chris Pappas

November ballot. We did it. Thank you for playing your part in getting

questions or concerns:

name: Autism Health
subject: Join Our Monthly Autism Support Group...
body:
** Join Us for Our Monthly Autism Support Group
------------------------------------------------------------

We invite you to join us for our upcoming Autism Support Group on Tuesday, July 14th at 5 PM PST / 8 PM EST via Zoom. Whether you are a parent, caregiver, family member, self advocate, or professional, this monthly gathering offers a welcoming space to connect with others who understand the autism journey.

Our support group provides an opportunity to share experiences, ask questions, exchange resources, and receive encouragement from a compassionate community. Together, we discuss the challenges and victories that come with raising and supporting individuals with autism and related neurological conditions, while learning from one another in a respectful and supportive environment.

This is more than a meeting. It is a community where families can build meaningful connections, gain practical insights, and know they are not alone on this journey.

Advance registration is required to attend. Please register using the link below to receive your Zoom access information.

We look forward to seeing you there!
REGISTER HERE (https://us06web.zoom.us/meeting/register/xQxg3Z3QSCybI3_aGxmUkA?mc_cid=3eb2f09fab&mc_eid=UNIQID#/registration)

** Save the Date: Cocktails for A Cause
------------------------------------------------------------

We are excited to invite you to our upcoming Cocktails for A Cause fundraiser benefiting Autism Health Inc. on Wednesday, August 5, 2026, from 6:00 PM to 8:00 PM at The Park Club in Costa Mesa, CA.

Sponsored by Cellular Performance Institute, this special evening will bring together supporters, families, professionals, and community leaders for a night of connection, purpose, and giving back. Guests will enjoy cocktails, networking, an inspiring presentation from Dr. Dayan Goodenowe, and both a live auction and silent auction filled with exciting items and experiences.

Tickets are $85 per person, and proceeds from the evening will help support Autism Health Inc.’s ongoing mission to provide education, resources, support programs, and outreach for families impacted by autism and neurological conditions.

We hope you will join us for this meaningful evening as we come together to make a difference in the lives of so many families.
BUY TICKETS HERE (https://givebutter.com/cocktails-4-a-cause?gbtid=364872ca-6248-4fff-badb-efb5ca682c2c&mc_cid=3eb2f09fab&mc_eid=UNIQID)

** Don't Miss Out on this Spectacular Savings!
------------------------------------------------------------

Save 50% on the 2027 Autism Health Summit This July!

There has never been a better time to reserve your seat for the 2027 Autism Health Summit! Throughout the month of July only, receive 50% OFF your in person admission with promo code AHS50.

Join us April 29 through May 1, 2027, at the beautiful Legacy Center Resort & Spa in San Diego, California, for three inspiring days of education, collaboration, and community. The Autism Health Summit brings together leading physicians, researchers, practitioners, advocates, and families from around the world to explore the latest advances in autism research, integrative medicine, and whole person health. This exclusive offer ends July 31st and will not be available again, so reserve your seat today.

As part of our mission to make education accessible to everyone, Autism Health Inc. proudly offers scholarships for low and middle income families who may not otherwise be able to attend. We believe every family deserves access to trusted education, resources, and a supportive community, regardless of financial circumstances. You can access the application on our website.

Register today and learn more using the links below.
REGISTER HERE (https://ahsconference.com/pricing-table/?mc_cid=3eb2f09fab&mc_eid=UNIQID)
Are you interested in partnering with Autism Health? During the month of July, organizations can also receive 10% OFF all 2027 sponsorship packages by using promo code Sponsor10. This is the perfect opportunity to showcase your organization while supporting one of the nation's premier autism education conferences.
REGISTER HERE (https://ahsconference.com/sponsors/?mc_cid=3eb2f09fab&mc_eid=UNIQID)

** Summer Movie Fundraiser
------------------------------------------------------------

Looking for a fun way to support Autism Health this summer? We are excited to partner with GroupRaise and Regal Cinemas for a special fundraising campaign that allows you to enjoy a night at the movies while supporting a great cause.

For just $30 per order, you'll receive a Regal Movie Ticket Bundle that includes two Standard 2D Movie Tickets, redeemable at any Regal theater location nationwide. Best of all, 20% of every purchase will be donated to Autism Health Inc. to help support our educational programs, support groups, webinars, scholarships, and research initiatives.

Did you know that many Regal Cinemas locations also offer Sensory Friendly Screenings? These special screenings are designed to create a more comfortable movie-going experience for individuals with autism and sensory sensitivities, making this fundraiser even more meaningful for our community.

Whether you're planning a family outing, date night, or looking for a unique gift, your purchase helps advance our mission of serving individuals and families impacted by autism and related neurological conditions.

Campaign Ends: Monday, August 17, 2026

Thank you for supporting Autism Health Inc. Every ticket bundle purchased helps us continue making a difference in the lives of families around the world.
BUY TICKETS HERE (https://www.groupraise.com/offer-campaigns/78957-autism-health-inc-regal-fundraising-campaigns?mc_cid=3eb2f09fab&mc_eid=UNIQID)

Please Vote for the 2026 Author of the Year

We are honored to share that Tracy Slepcevic, Co-Founder and President of Autism Health Inc., has been nominated for the 2026 Author of the Year award through the International Impact Book Awards.

Tracy’s bestselling book, Warrior Mom: A Mother's Journey in Healing Her Son with Autism, has inspired and empowered families around the world through her heartfelt story of perseverance, faith, and determination as a mother navigating the autism journey. More than just a memoir, Warrior Mom has become a trusted guidebook for parents seeking hope, practical insight, and encouragement while advocating for their children.

The book has received praise from many respected voices, including the endorsement from Robert F. Kennedy Jr., who described Warrior Mom as:
“An inspiring testimony to the miraculous power of maternal love.”

We would deeply appreciate your support in helping recognize Tracy’s impact and dedication to the autism community. Voting closes on August 31, 2026, and every vote makes a difference.

Learn more about Warrior Mom at: www.WarriorMom.com (https://track.pstmrk.it/3s/links.givebutter.com%2Fengage%2FBwmn%2FngDgvqQ/b43o/ZIrGAQ/AQ/60384151-45bf-40df-96e9-14b6fd8b5f67/6/CKEGI8ajt-?mc_cid=3eb2f09fab&mc_eid=UNIQID)

VOTE HERE (https://apply.internationalimpactbookawards.com/public-voting-form?mc_cid=3eb2f09fab&mc_eid=UNIQID)

About Autism Health Inc.
Autism Health is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization dedicated to educating individuals, families, and communities about autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Autism Health provides educational programs, workshops, events, research, and resources tailored to meet the diverse needs of those impacted by autism and other neurological disorders.
DONATE HERE (https://autismhealth.com/donations/?mc_cid=3eb2f09fab&mc_eid=UNIQID)
Autism Health Inc. depends on generous donations from our community. Large or small, every donation gets us closer to achieving our goals. We are grateful for your assistance! For more information about Autism Health, visit www.AutismHealth.com

Mike Lawler has faced Democratic politicians before. But he’s never faced someone like me. He and I are about the same age. We both grew up in the Hudson Valley. And for the last twenty years, while he’s been a political hack and operative, scheming and maneuvering, I’ve been leading America’s sons and daughters in defense of this nation. I went to West Point after 9/11. I spent 16 years in the Army, deployed six times overseas, and served as Director for Counterterrorism at the White House. **My life has been about service to our country and to our community.** And it is very clear that this administration, and the cowards like Mike Lawler who enable it, do not care about our country or share our values – or the values of the generations of Americans who fought and sacrificed to make this country better. | | | **FROM THE DESK OF JEFF HURD** **COLORADO** July 7, 2026
---
| | Thank you, Colorado!

Because of your support, your hard work, and your prayers, we won our Primary Election. I couldn’t be more grateful. From the beginning, this campaign has been about standing up for the people who make rural America strong. It’s been about fighting for the farmers, ranchers, small businesses, energy producers, and most importantly, the families of Western and Southern Colorado. It’s been about putting Colorado first, every single day. Now, our focus turns to November. And the choice ahead couldn’t be clearer: a proven conservative who gets real results for the Western Slope, or a Democrat whose policies would drive up costs, undermine our energy security, and leave rural America behind. There’s still a lot of work ahead, but with your continued support, I know we will finish what we started.

Thank you for believing in this campaign and for standing with me. I’m honored to have your trust, and I’ll keep fighting every single day to put Colorado first. To victory,

DEAR FRIENDS,

Our campaign is ramping up fast, and I'm excited to share the great progress we're making together. Signature collection is going
strong, and we're getting closer every day to getting on the ballot. If you haven't signed yet, please stop by our headquarters in
Warwick 205 Buttonwoods Ave, Warwick, RI.

Last week we had an incredible cookout in Bristol for veterans and community members. Live music, great food, and my wife and kids
were right there with me. It was a wonderful day talking with so many good, hardworking people who love this state and this
country. The Vic Mellor campaign marched in the Ancient and Horribles parade, and the crowd was incredible, full of energy and
patriotism.

As we head deeper into summer, we're ramping up even more. We'll be visiting small businesses across the district, listening to
owners about the real challenges they face and the successes they're fighting for. Rhode Island has been dead last in too many
categories for far too long. It's time we finally put Rhode Island first by creating an environment where good jobs can grow and
small businesses can thrive again.

July 4th always reminds us how precious our freedom really is. It reminds us that our freedom was never guaranteed — it was
earned, and it must be defended. Benjamin Franklin was asked what kind of government we had created. He answered, "A republic, if
you can keep it." That warning rings true today. We need to rededicate ourselves to the American way of life and the American
Dream, the belief that if you work hard, you can build a better life for yourself and your family.

I am proud to be an American. I am thankful every single day to live in the greatest country the world has ever known. While Seth
Magaziner and his party push an anti-American agenda that teaches our kids to be ashamed of this country, I will always stand up
for the values, the history, and the people that made America exceptional. We will not apologize for loving our flag, our
Constitution, or our freedom.

This campaign is about putting Rhode Island first and fighting for the America we believe in. If you're tired of being last, if
you're tired of politicians who divide us and tear down our country, then join us. Stop by headquarters, sign a petition, grab a
sign, or just come say hello.

Together we're going to bring real change.

God bless you, God bless Rhode Island, and God bless the United States of America.

Sincerely,

Vic Mellor

Candidate for Congress, Rhode Island's 2nd District

clean_body: [] DEAR FRIENDS, Our campaign is ramping up fast, and I'm excited to share the great progress we're making together. Signature collection is going strong, and we're getting closer every day to getting on the ballot. If you haven't signed yet, please stop by our headquarters in Warwick 205 Buttonwoods Ave, Warwick, RI. Last week we had an incredible cookout in Bristol for veterans and community members. Live music, great food, and my wife and kids were right there with me. It was a wonderful day talking with so many good, hardworking people who love this state and this country. The Vic Mellor campaign marched in the Ancient and Horribles parade, and the crowd was incredible, full of energy and patriotism. As we head deeper into summer, we're ramping up even more. We'll be visiting small businesses across the district, listening to owners about the real challenges they face and the successes they're fighting for. Rhode Island has been dead last in too many categories for far too long. It's time we finally put Rhode Island first by creating an environment where good jobs can grow and small businesses can thrive again. July 4th always reminds us how precious our freedom really is. It reminds us that our freedom was never guaranteed — it was earned, and it must be defended. Benjamin Franklin was asked what kind of government we had created. He answered, "A republic, if you can keep it." That warning rings true today. We need to rededicate ourselves to the American way of life and the American Dream, the belief that if you work hard, you can build a better life for yourself and your family. I am proud to be an American. I am thankful every single day to live in the greatest country the world has ever known. While Seth Magaziner and his party push an anti-American agenda that teaches our kids to be ashamed of this country, I will always stand up for the values, the history, and the people that made America exceptional. We will not apologize for loving our flag, our Constitution, or our freedom. This campaign is about putting Rhode Island first and fighting for the America we believe in. If you're tired of being last, if you're tired of politicians who divide us and tear down our country, then join us. Stop by headquarters, sign a petition, grab a sign, or just come say hello. Together we're going to bring real change. God bless you, God bless Rhode Island, and God bless the United States of America. Sincerely, Vic Mellor Candidate for Congress, Rhode Island's 2nd District [] [] [] [] [] [] [] Want to change how you receive these emails?

clean_body: RSVP to our Powered by One Cup Community Call | | | Peter, what has been your favorite moment of this World Cup? ⚽ From the world rallying behind Cabo Verde and Vozinha to European tourists discovering the wonders of ranch dressing, this World Cup has taught us that the only divide being created between us is by those in power. This celebration of unity belongs to us, the people. The people have the power and we're fighting for a future where we can ALL THRIVE! 📣 Will you join us at our “Powered by One Cup” Monthly Community Call on Wednesday, July 15, at 7 pm ET to learn how to call for a pathway to citizenship for millions of working people who power the World Cup and our country? \---------- Forwarded message --------- From: Matias, United We Dream Date: Fri, Jul 3, 2026 at 1:35 PM Subject: 🏆 RSVP NOW: Powered by One Cup ¿Y si sí, Peter? What if we really are capable of building something bigger than this? 👀 Right now, they’re treating us - the people - like we’re disposable. Immigration agents are disappearing our neighbors off the street, while the rest of us struggle to make ends meet. From the DACA recipient teacher waiting for her work authorization to be renewed, to the stadium worker going home at the end of the match with mounting bills to pay, ALL of us have had enough. But, together, we can build a future where our families have the safety and stability we need. One where we don’t have to wait from court decision to court decision to determine our fate. This summer, the entire globe has got its eyes on the World Cup. We’ve been able to connect across cultures and languages to root for one another. This celebration of unity belongs to us, the people. This celebration belongs to the tens of thousands of working people who are behind the scenes making this event happen. From stadium workers to hotel staff, the World Cup is powered by the hands of everyday people. And, this country cannot continue to deny our neighbors the stability and safety they need. 📣 Will you join us at our “Powered by One Cup” Monthly Community Call on Wednesday, July 15, at 7 pm ET to learn how to call for a pathway to citizenship for millions of working people who power the World Cup and our country? ****This World Cup, the real win for ALL of us is a pathway to citizenship that keeps our communities whole. The same spirit of connection that brings us together in the stands must unite us in our call for citizenship! True solidarity means protecting those who power our celebrations, not treating them as expendable. At our community call, you’ll connect with neighbors across the country who feel the same way as you and learn how to turn this spirit of solidarity into real action. 🧡 In unity, Matias and the UWD team | Follow us on: | | | | |

Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Graham Platner speaks at his Primary Election event on June 9, 2026 in Blue Hill, Maine. Photo by CJ Gunther/Getty Images.
Since announcing his run almost a year ago, Graham Platner's source of strength was his ability to organize people passionately committed to building a populist movement centered on the needs of working people. The energy behind this politics of change is genuinely real and organic. Thousands of people have volunteered their time to Platner's cause across every county in Maine.
But after [allegations of rape](https://substack.com/redirect/5b2e36e2-8a7a-4224-b015-5c72a0aa7f8d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) against Platner broke yesterday, many of those volunteer workers no longer believe he is the right standard bearer for the movement they've been working so hard to build. The victim, Jenny Racicot, told Politico that Platner broke into her home in 2021 while drunk and began forcing himself on her. Racicot said she tried to separate herself from Platner but that he followed her to her bedroom and raped her.
Drop Site spoke with numerous Platner volunteers to determine where Maine's rapidly growing populist base might be headed. Overwhelmingly, supporters are ready to move on from Platner while remaining emboldened to continue their work building the grassroots movement that he jump-started.

He has been working with the campaign at almost every event and town hall since its beginning. If Platner does drop out, he would "really like to see Troy Jackson get the nod" as replacement.
Patrick Reis, 29, a volunteer from Portland, described himself to Drop Site as a "hardcore Platner supporter" who has been working with the campaign since the first town hall. "Platner often said he was building a movement to outlast him or carry on in his absence. I bet he thought that time would come years from now, but it's upon us," Reis said. They believe any replacement must be "another working class candidate who comes out of the movement," and would "wholeheartedly" throw their support behind Troy Jackson.
"This has been about working Mainers rejecting a politics that doesn't serve them," Darnall-Hirani added.
In county-level Platner Signal groups, volunteers driving the door knocking, canvassing, and tabling efforts in their respective regions repeatedly expressed how they were "struggling" and "incredibly upset." Multiple volunteers said the story was "painful" to read. One volunteer leader noted that no volunteer "staff members had been involved in conversations nor did anyone receive advanced notice" about the story before it broke.
"Whatever happens, I would like to keep our group chat alive. Anger told Drop Site she has been involved in Platner's campaign for the policies, not the candidate. She considers it a tragedy that electoral politics require that we marry our policy demands to a single human being.
"The important thing is we are all still here. What we are demanding of our government has not and will not change. We just have to persist and fight for policies we support, regardless of what person we elect to carry out or will in office," Anger added.
"For the moment, group leaders and volunteers are focusing on being there for each other and keeping our contacts and the friends we've made supporting this campaign together. We're focused on advancing progressive policy," Mihalovits said. "This was never about a single candidate, but about all of us working together for a better vision than Susan Collins ever offered Maine."
Morgan, a male volunteer in the Central Maine Signal group, told Drop Site that compelling sexual assault allegations must always be a red line, regardless of how they surface and from whom. He has been with the campaign "since day one," canvassing, phonebanking, and volunteering at town halls.
He said Platner "needs to do the right thing and step down, and actively encourage his volunteers to channel their incredible energy and organization into the next leader who will carry our platform forward."
"This campaign represents an unprecedented investment of my time and energy. I didn't do it for a single candidate," Morgan said. "I believe our policy platform is bigger than Graham Platner. It is a vision that transcends any one man, and I have faith that we can nominate a leader who will carry that vision forward, and wield the power that comes with it."

[](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyskDuO4zAQRE9DZTaaH5FUwGABw5k33VCg1S2LACUKZK8_tx9oojnAZA-oqhfUv9t4iymn7fE3rhT4PZcRCdMUmXDc6NUyMVMdX8snVmpljdsHa3pSbe0_Im2jAmVP4E7gfixlh-EOOMiOgnReG-OM6bsloCdr7wqU7OPgYMA5TprAWW1ISfBdCocQHDjpQffDufeznbUiUB7JeC0MECYu9cwLMb1jm_OnPKmep7J2OSzMexP6j1BXoa57LUwTE5adU9naUToSfY1CX6TxvVB2OtB7dXCTQl-6GnB_pZxTs04YeKwx5W8__-ZHz6C-AgAA__82nH5b) And the differences can be surprisingly large. Voter Action Project[https://voteractionproject.org/]
Donald Trump is demanding -- again -- that Congress pass the SAVE America Act (the latest version of the anti-voting SAVE Act). With the House set to pass it again this week, the Senate is all we have left to stop this suppressive legislation from becoming law ahead of the midterm elections, folks.

Defenders of voting rights know that non-citizen voting is already illegal, extremely rare, and that this bill is written in a way that could disenfranchise millions of eligible women across the country. Here's Colorado Senator Michael Bennet on the impact of these bills:
(Image of Michael Bennet speaking on the Senate floor) [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/EA/EA007/1/89215/images/SAVE_MB.jpg]
Opponents of voting rights in Congress -- and in the White House -- favor this bill because they know it could suppress millions of eligible voters, changing the composition of the electorate and potentially empowering them and their party for years to come.
Please, Team, join these brave Senators today. Fuel our efforts to stop this dangerous legislation with $25 or whatever you can and ensure millions of women's voices continue to be heard in our elections >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=070726_2&amount=25]
If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:
GIVE $15 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=070726_2&amount=15] GIVE $25 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=070726_2&amount=25] GIVE $50 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?express_lane=true&refcode=070726_2&amount=50]

We know the SAVE Act was fast-tracked by opponents of voting rights to be in place before the next election, folks. This bill is a stunning assault on our fundamental right to vote, and we can not afford to let this anti-democratic legislation become law.
If you missed it: This bill would force every voter to present proof of citizenship to register, either a passport or a birth certificate that matches their current first and last name -- something millions of eligible American women don’t have. And that’s the point.
The bill would also obliterate popular methods of voter registration for all voters, including:
* Registration by mail

* 3rd party voter registration drives

* Online voter registration in states that allow it

* Automatic voter registration
Some estimates say that this bill could disenfranchise anywhere from 11 million to 65 million eligible Americans , especially women and those who live in under-resourced communities.
“ There’s never been an attack on voting rights out of Congress like this ,” said Alexander Keyssar, a professor of History and Social Policy at the Harvard Kennedy School, and a leading historian of voting rights. “ It’s always been the federal government trying to keep states in check on voting rights, for the most part. ”

| | Patriot,
---
I'm going to be blunt with you.

We are closer to losing this country than most people are willing to admit.

Not someday. Not "if things keep going this way."

Right now.

And the scariest part?

It's not happening in Washington. It's happening in classrooms.

High schools. Colleges.

Places where the next generation is being shaped -- or more accurately... reshaped.

If you've ever looked at what's coming out of our schools and thought: _" What happened to this country?" _

You're not wrong. You're seeing it clearly.

Because while most people are arguing online... while they're hoping things will turn around... while they're waiting for the next election to fix everything...

The other side is doing something far more dangerous.

They're raising the next generation.

Earlier. Faster. And with zero resistance in most places.

That's how countries are lost.

Slowly. Then all at once.

But here's the thing that should give a patriot like you hope...

There is one place where that trend is actually being challenged.

_And it shouldn 't even exist. _

**Just one year ago, Turning Point USA 's high school program -- which is now called "Club America" -- was in about 1,200 schools.**
That alone felt like a miracle.

Because starting even ONE chapter today takes courage most adults don't have.

Conservative students get mocked. Targeted. Threatened. Shut down.

And yet...

_They stepped up anyway. _

About that time, Charlie called me.

He didn't sound optimistic... He sounded urgent.

"Andrew, we've got to move faster."

I told him we were. He stopped me.

"No. You're not thinking what I'm thinking. I want to be in 35,000 high schools."

I actually laughed.

"Charlie... there aren't even 35,000 high schools in America."

"Okay," he said. "How many are there?"

"About 27,000."

And without hesitation: "Good. Let's do 27,000."

I remember sitting there thinking to myself... we're barely in 1,200 schools.

We didn't have the staff. We didn't have the infrastructure. We didn't even have the roadmap yet.

But Charlie wasn't fazed.

_" We'll figure it out." _

That was him.

He didn't wait for perfect conditions.

Because he knew something most people don't want to face: If we wait... _we lose everything. _

And now?

Less than a year later...

**We 're in 3,300 schools. **

**Thirteen percent of all high schools in America. **

**Eight states are now backing this effort to put a Club America chapter in every high school statewide. **

_That shouldn 't be possible. _

Not in this environment. Not with the level of hostility these students face every single day.

And yet... it's still happening.

_But Patriot, here 's the part you need to understand: _

This is not a victory. It's a foothold.

_Because in the other 87% of schools? _

There is no resistance. None.

Just one-sided propaganda from the Left.

One-sided pressure on kids who are too young to even realize what's happening to them.

That's the reality.

The question isn't whether we're fighting. We are.

The question is whether it's enough.

Because right now, the students stepping up through Club America...

They're not the majority. _They 're the exception. _

They're the ones willing to take the heat.

The ones willing to stand alone.

The ones willing to risk being targeted just to say: _" I love this country." _

And every time one of those students raises their hand...

We have a choice.

Back them. _Or leave them on their own. _

**Because when a student starts a chapter, we send them an activism kit -- with American flags. Pocket Constitutions. Leadership tools. **

Everything they need to actually stand their ground.

Not symbolically. For real.

They've already made the decision to lead.

All they're waiting on... is you and me.

**Each activism kit costs $25. That 's it. **

$25 to make sure one student doesn't have to stand alone against the Left in a hostile school.

$25 to put real tools in their hands.

$25 to push back -- even if it's one campus at a time.

They're choosing courage in places designed to make them conform.

And they're not alone.

They're finding each other. They're bringing more students with them every day.

They're building something real -- rooted in faith and freedom, grounded in truth, and unafraid to say that America is worth defending.

Not "if things keep going this way." Right now. And the scariest part? It's not happening in Washington. It's happening in classrooms. High schools. Colleges. Places where the next generation is being shaped -- or more accurately... reshaped. If you've ever looked at what's coming out of our schools and thought: " What happened to this country?" You're not wrong. You're seeing it clearly. Because while most people are arguing online... while they're hoping things will turn around... while they're waiting for the next election to fix everything... The other side is doing something far more dangerous. They're raising the next generation. Earlier. Faster. And with zero resistance in most places. That's how countries are lost. Slowly. Then all at once. But here's the thing that should give a patriot like you hope... There is one place where that trend is actually being challenged. And it shouldn 't even exist. Just one year ago, Turning Point USA 's high school program -- which is now called "Club America" -- was in about 1,200 schools. That alone felt like a miracle. Because starting even ONE chapter today takes courage most adults don't have. Conservative students get mocked. Targeted. Threatened. Shut down. And yet... They stepped up anyway. About that time, Charlie called me. He didn't sound optimistic... He sounded urgent. "Andrew, we've got to move faster." I told him we were. He stopped me. "No. You're not thinking what I'm thinking. I want to be in 35,000 high schools." I actually laughed. "Charlie... there aren't even 35,000 high schools in America." "Okay," he said. "How many are there?" "About 27,000." And without hesitation: "Good. Let's do 27,000." I remember sitting there thinking to myself... we're barely in 1,200 schools. We didn't have the staff. We didn't have the infrastructure. I spent fifteen years wearing a badge and a uniform, protecting the halls of the United States Capitol. On January 6th, I saw firsthand what happens when people abandon their decency for a cult of personality. I saw what happens when the "ends justify the means" becomes a way of life. But as I've transitioned from the front lines of law enforcement to the arena of politics, advocating for the soul of this Nation, I've realized that the erosion of our moral compass isn't just a "them" problem. It's a humanity problem that cuts across the aisles and transcends policitics and its here at our front door.
We in the Democratic base are often so desperate for a hero, so eager for a bold leader who will stand up to the MAGA faction that we become willing to overlook the rot underneath the surface. We see a man who speaks the right language of justice, truth and fairness, and we hand him our trust without checking his character. But character isn't what you say when the cameras are rolling; it's how you treat people when you THINK no one is watching. And lately, too many men in our ranks have proven that their public persona is nothing more than a mask.
Look at the trail of scandals we've been asked to ignore or "contextualize" away. We saw the downfall of Andrew Cuomo, a man who was once hailed as the gold standard of leadership, only for the world to find a pattern of harassment and a toxic culture of intimidation. What we're seeing with Graham Platner situation. Whether we're excusing his "lack of knowledge" for getting a Nazi tattoo, or him being too forceful with past partners, or wether he raped Ms. Racicot. We are now forced to make a decision if fighting for a progressive future "trumps" personal conduct. We remember John Edwards, a man who ran on "Two Americas" while leading a double life that mocked the very family values he preached. And then there is Eric Swalwell here is the reoccurring theme: men in power thinking the rules of common decency and CONSENT don't apply to them because they are on the right side of wanting to "save our democracy"
When we throw our unwavering support behind these flawed men just because they wear blue instead of red, how are we any different from those in the MAGA cult? We rightfully point out the hypocrisy of those who support Donald Trump, a man found liable for sexual assault and named more times in the Epstein files than Jesus is in the bible; yet we find ourselves making excuses for our own "champions" because we're afraid of losing a seat. If we argue that "our guy" is better because his policy is better, while his conduct is just as predatory or deceptive, we've already lost something greater than an election.
I've always said that I believe in the truth and part of that truth is a firm, unwavering stance: I believe women. I believe victims of sexual assault. I believe them regardless of how many years have passed, and I believe them even if they carry their trauma to the grave. We live in a climate where a woman can come forward with a sombering truth, and somehow, through the "art" of political spin or the magic of social media, she becomes the villain. It is ass-backwards to claim we are the party of women's rights while we silence the women who find the courage to speak up against men in our own ranks.
The phrase "Vote Blue No Matter Who" was meant to be a rallying cry for unity, but it has been weaponized (I hate that word because Republicans use it so aimlessly) into a shield for the mediocre and the manipulative. If the "Who" is a man who lacks basic decency, who treats women as property, and who lies to the public about his true character, then that "Who" doesn't deserve your vote. We cannot protect democracy with leaders who have no integrity. The ends do not justify the means if, by the time we reach the end, we have sacrificed the very values we were supposed to be fighting for. We have to be better. We have to demand better. Because if we lose our moral compass, we've already lost the country.

clean_body: The Moral High Ground should not be treated as a Campaign Slogan | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more The Moral High Ground should not be treated as a Campaign Slogan | | | Jul 7 | | | | | | | | | | | | I spent fifteen years wearing a badge and a uniform, protecting the halls of the United States Capitol. On January 6th, I saw firsthand what happens when people abandon their decency for a cult of personality. I saw what happens when the "ends justify the means" becomes a way of life. But as I've transitioned from the front lines of law enforcement to the arena of politics, advocating for the soul of this Nation, I've realized that the erosion of our moral compass isn't just a "them" problem. It's a humanity problem that cuts across the aisles and transcends policitics and its here at our front door. We in the Democratic base are often so desperate for a hero, so eager for a bold leader who will stand up to the MAGA faction that we become willing to overlook the rot underneath the surface. We see a man who speaks the right language of justice, truth and fairness, and we hand him our trust without checking his character. But character isn't what you say when the cameras are rolling; it's how you treat people when you THINK no one is watching. And lately, too many men in our ranks have proven that their public persona is nothing more than a mask. Look at the trail of scandals we've been asked to ignore or "contextualize" away. We saw the downfall of Andrew Cuomo, a man who was once hailed as the gold standard of leadership, only for the world to find a pattern of harassment and a toxic culture of intimidation. What we're seeing with Graham Platner situation. Whether we're excusing his "lack of knowledge" for getting a Nazi tattoo, or him being too forceful with past partners, or wether he raped Ms. Racicot. We are now forced to make a decision if fighting for a progressive future "trumps" personal conduct. We remember John Edwards, a man who ran on "Two Americas" while leading a double life that mocked the very family values he preached. And then there is Eric Swalwell here is the reoccurring theme: men in power thinking the rules of common decency and CONSENT don't apply to them because they are on the right side of wanting to "save our democracy" When we throw our unwavering support behind these flawed men just because they wear blue instead of red, how are we any different from those in the MAGA cult? We rightfully point out the hypocrisy of those who support Donald Trump, a man found liable for sexual assault and named more times in the Epstein files than Jesus is in the bible; yet we find ourselves making excuses for our own "champions" because we're afraid of losing a seat. If we argue that "our guy" is better because his policy is better, while his conduct is just as predatory or deceptive, we've already lost something greater than an election. I've always said that I believe in the truth and part of that truth is a firm, unwavering stance: I believe women. I believe victims of sexual assault. I believe them regardless of how many years have passed, and I believe them even if they carry their trauma to the grave. We live in a climate where a woman can come forward with a sombering truth, and somehow, through the "art" of political spin or the magic of social media, she becomes the villain. It is ass-backwards to claim we are the party of women's rights while we silence the women who find the courage to speak up against men in our own ranks. The phrase "Vote Blue No Matter Who" was meant to be a rallying cry for unity, but it has been weaponized (I hate that word because Republicans use it so aimlessly) into a shield for the mediocre and the manipulative. If the "Who" is a man who lacks basic decency, who treats women as property, and who lies to the public about his true character, then that "Who" doesn't deserve your vote. We cannot protect democracy with leaders who have no integrity. The ends do not justify the means if, by the time we reach the end, we have sacrificed the very values we were supposed to be fighting for. We have to be better. We have to demand better. Because if we lose our moral compass, we've already lost the country. You're currently a free subscriber to . | | | | Hey Friend,
Last week the Supreme Court ruled that states can protect fairness in women's sports by keeping competition based on biological sex. **Suhas Subramanyam** already told VA-10 families where he stands: back in January of 2025, he **voted no on the Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act.**
That vote came a year and a half before the Supreme Court weighed in, and it still stands on the record today. I believe every young woman who has trained her whole life for a fair shot at a scholarship or a title deserves a level playing field, and I will never vote to take that away.
**If you want a congressman who will always fight for the rights of women and girls to compete fairly, I would be honored to earn your vote.**
_**[DONATE TO DAVE](https://link.mail.beckwithforcongress.)**_
In Congress, I will always vote to protect fair competition for women and girls, and I will not apologize for it. This is not a complicated issue. Fairness means competing on a level field, and I will defend that every time it comes to a vote.
Families across Loudoun, Fairfax, Prince William, and every corner of VA-10 deserve a representative who stands up for their daughters before the cameras are rolling, not only after the Supreme Court forces the issue.
Primary day is August 4th, and early voting is open right now. Help me finish strong by chipping in today.
_**[DONATE TO DAVE](https://link.mail.beckwithforcongress.)**_
As someone who has raised a daughter, this fight is close to home. It is exactly what I would want any member of Congress to do if it were my own daughter's future on the line.
---
| | | God Bless, Dave Beckwith
**Beckwith for Congress** _Safe. Strong. Responsible._

_P.S. — Suhas voted no in January of 2025, the Supreme Court said otherwise in June of 2026, and I am asking for you to help elect a congressman who will not wait on the courts to do what is right.___

Peter,

My name’s Troy Downing. When America faced its darkest hour after 9/11, I knew I couldn't just sit on the sidelines. I enlisted in the U.S. Air Force and served eight years in a Combat Search and Rescue squadron, deploying twice to Afghanistan.

subject: From "idiot" to genius overnight

A Special Message from our SponsorPlease note that views expressed in this message do not necessarily reflect those of Free Speech Daily and do not constitute an endorsement or recommendation by Free Speech Daily.
I told you so
A few months ago, my neighbor Mark (not his real name) came pounding on my front door like the world was ending.

I opened it, but before I could even say hello, he blurted out:

"Have you BEEN to the grocery stores?!"

He looked panicked.

"The storm hit, everybody's freaking out, people are panic-buying everything and shelves are EMPTY. You need to go NOW before there's nothing left."

I just looked at him and said:

"I'm good."

That answer hit him like gasoline on a fire.

"What do you mean you're GOOD?" he snapped. "There's no food left!"

"I'm good," I repeated calmly.

Now he looked angry... and confused.

"Dude," he said, "didn't you hear what I just said?"

I didn't really want to explain myself.

But he kept pushing.

Finally, I sighed and said:

"Mark... remember that HOA meeting a few years back?"

His expression changed instantly.

"You overheard me talking to another neighbor about the emergency food kits I bought for my family."

I paused.

"And you called me an idiot. Said I sounded like some conspiracy theorist."

Immediately, he started backpedaling.

"I never said–"

Then he stopped cold.

Because he remembered.

I watched his face change right in front of me.

The confidence disappeared.

His shoulders sank.

And quietly, almost embarrassed, he said:

"... I did say that."

Neither of us spoke for a few seconds.

Then he looked me dead in the eye and said:

"Man, I was wrong. I'm sorry."

I nodded.

"Mark, the reason I'm not panicking right now is simple..."

"I prepared before everyone else did."

"While people were laughing, I quietly made sure my family would be okay no matter what happened."

I told him we had months of emergency food stored away.

Enough to feed my entire family.

No panic.

No stress.

No fighting crowds.

No wondering how we'd survive if things got worse.

You could tell the whole experience rattled him, and I could see he was already thinking about his wife and kids.

The fear in his voice was gone now.

Before he left, he asked me to send him the exact food kits we trusted for our family.

## Campaign Update
Nate Launches Ad Campaign Targeting Rigged Economy, Corporate Special Interests
* We are starting to launch a new ad campaign taking direct aim at the corporate interests and rigged economic system Nate believes are failing Eastern Washington's working families.
* The ads come as incumbent Republican Michael Baumgartner faces growing scrutiny over his votes to cut Medicaid and his support for legislation that would block Washington state from regulating AI data centers for five years, even as Avista negotiates a deal that could draw 500 megawatts of power for a new data center in the region.
* The ads will run on television, streaming, and social media.
* Please like and share the ads with friends and family when you see them!

While the Trump administration and RFK Jr. undermine vaccine safety from Washington, states like Colorado are stepping up to protect public health.
And Georgia could be doing the same — with the right leadership.
As a scientist and someone who has spent my time in office fighting for evidence-based policy, it breaks my heart to watch politicians play games with public health. Casting doubt on vaccine safety doesn’t just create confusion — it leads to real harm, especially for children, seniors, and immunocompromised families.
Colorado is showing what responsible leadership looks like: putting science first, protecting access, and ensuring communities stay safe.
Georgia deserves nothing less.
That’s why I’m asking you to add your name to my petition calling on Georgia lawmakers to defend vaccine access, reject political interference, and stand firmly with science.
We can build a state where our leaders protect families instead of pandering to conspiracy theorists — but only if we make our voices impossible to ignore.

Last week, we filed our 73rd lawsuit against the Trump administration — this time to stop their unlawful and unconstitutional Medicaid work requirements that threaten to strip healthcare from the 20 million Americans who rely on the program nationwide.
Time and again, the Trump administration has pursued policies that threaten the most vulnerable among us. As I’ve said before, when they break the law and harm Californians, we'll take them to court.
If you want to continue supporting this work, please consider chipping in to my re-election campaign by clicking here. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26]
Last month, the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) and the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) published a rule that makes it harder for vulnerable people to access the care they need, rips coverage from people who need it, and increases healthcare costs. This rule will exclude the kinds of people that Medicaid was created to cover — people with severe illnesses and disabilities, people in the middle of cancer treatment, people who are blind, people who have a disabling mental health condition.
In fact, Congress created exclusions from Medicaid’s work requirements to ensure that people with complex illnesses and disabilities don’t lose coverage or have interruptions in care.
We’ve seen what happens when unnecessary barriers are added to Medicaid. Eligible people lose coverage; state-run programs, safety net providers, and emergency rooms absorb the strain; and costs go up as more residents become uninsured.
People living with serious illnesses or disabilities already face enormous challenges in their daily lives. They shouldn’t also have to fear losing their healthcare because of this administration’s unlawful and reckless policies.
I’m co-leading a coalition of 24 attorneys general and 2 governors in suing the Trump administration — because as Attorney General of California, I will never stop fighting to protect your healthcare.
If you’re with me, will you help power our work with a contribution right now? Anything you can give will have a meaningful impact on what we can accomplish together. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rb-email-26]

body:
# [](https://act.betoorourke.com/go/43706?t=1&akid=240941%2E444211%2EJG5Uuh)
If you want to end this MAGA nightmare... if you want James Talarico to be the next senator from the state of Texas... if you want to take it to Ken Paxton... this one is for you.
**You probably remember that Paxton came after me and Powered by People in the middle of the Texas gerrymandering fight last year.**
He sued us not because we’d broken any law, but because he hoped that bringing the full weight of the Attorney General’s office against us would cause us to throw in the towel. He was rightfully worried that our grassroots organizing, voter registration programs and our willingness to fight to the last breath against this attempted authoritarian takeover of our government would cause him problems in his race for Senate.
Maybe, he thought, he could tie us up in courts, force us to rack up unaffordable legal bills, and sideline one of the most innovative voter turnout programs in the country.
It’s what he’s tried to do to other groups across the state. Annunciation House. FIEL Houston. Catholic Charities of the Rio Grande Valley. Jolt Initiative.
He even sued the Democratic donation processing firm ActBlue.
Not because anyone has broken the law. But because he sees them as political opponents.
Here’s the good news. Like us, many of these groups are fighting back. And like us, many of them are winning. ActBlue recently won a major decision in federal court.
**That shows that standing up to a thug like Paxton, fighting back and fighting to win, works. So let’s keep it up.** Because, while we’ve won at the district court and appeals court levels, he is not letting up, hoping to wear us down and stop us from organizing.
It hasn't been easy -- we’ve spent more than $500,000 in legal fees fighting him so far -- but it's been possible thanks to contributions from people like you.

Beto

And President Trump is making it worse. _Housing costs have skyrocketed._ Since 2019, the median home price in New Mexico has climbed from $216,500 to $345,000. Rents have surged, too, and our state is still short roughly 40,000 affordable rental homes. _And New Mexico families are feeling it every single day._ That is why I worked with Democrats and Republicans to pass the bipartisan 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act — a package that would build more homes, help working families afford down payments, strengthen housing in rural communities, and stop corporate investors from buying up single-family homes that should be available to New Mexico families. **But President Trump has refused to sign it into law.** At a time when families need action, he's standing in the way of bipartisan solutions that would help bring down housing costs and expand homeownership. Hey Peter, it’s Drake — Aly’s campaign manager. There are a lot of serious things a campaign needs in order to win: A strong message. A great candidate. A plan to reach voters. Volunteers knocking doors, making calls, hosting events, and talking to their neighbors. **And then there are... lawn signs.** People _love_ lawn signs. They ask for them at events. They email about them. They text about them. They stop us in parking lots to ask when they can get one. And we love it. A lawn sign is one of the most visible ways to show your support for Aly!
