body:
No way out: Rural Colorado is outvoted at every turn
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**PRESENTED BY[ROCKYMOUNTAINVOICE.COM](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
| | Hey friends,
Want your full news breakdown? Listen to the Mountain Minute podcast [here](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), or watch on [YouTube](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) or [Rumble](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Also, check out today's [deep-dive video](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) on rural Colorado being outvoted at the Capitol.
Here's a summary of today's top stories:
**🏔️ Here in Colorado...** FEMA [approved aid for the Willow fire](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) (4,000 acres, 1% contained). Grand Junction [memorialized three firefighters](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) killed in the Snyder Fire. Despite a 36% auto theft drop, two Denver residents were [shot dead defending their cars](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), with Colorado still fourth-worst nationally. A feature detailed how [rural counties are outvoted despite GOP leanings](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), with the state Supreme Court barely blocking a Western Slope redistricting push. Complete Colorado reported [reading scores still lag](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) despite READ Act spending.
**🇺🇸 On the National Stage...** A Dallas Fed study found the 2021-2024 illegal immigration surge boosted employment but [drove 30% of home price increases](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) and 20% of rent hikes nationwide.
**🗣️ Commentary Spotlight...** O'Donnell's Part 2 flags [25,464 out-of-state movers still on Colorado's voter rolls](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) and $1.6M spent on undeliverable ballots. Pastor Drake Hunter urges [loving political adversaries](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.). Joondeph examines why [44% of under-40 voters now favor socialism](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), citing housing and wage pressures.
This is your Mountain Minute for Tuesday, July 7, 2026.
– Team RMV
---
|
---
**TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[No way out: Rural Colorado is outvoted at every turn](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
Tom Harrington manages a 500-cow operation on the Crystal River Ranch, two miles from the town of Carbondale on a mesa west of town. He grew up in Ridgway.
A friend sent him some papers from the North Park area of Walden showing the school news, a note from the old folks’ home and local ads. “I looked through these papers and I thought, man, this is like the 70s in Ridgway,” he said. Those things have disappeared from the Carbondale he lives in now. “They’ve certainly left here.”
He has also watched the valley floor transform in his 18 years on the ranch, hayfields replaced by a shopping complex and apartment buildings, the quiet gone with it. “Once things are paved over,” he said, “they never come back.”
What has also changed, for Harrington and for [Mesa County Board Chairman](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) JJ Fletcher, is who makes the decisions that shape their lives. In their experience, it is rarely anyone who has read a paper like that one from Walden, lost a calf to wolves or waited for a sheriff’s deputy on a dark ranch road.
**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|
---
**[Colorado’s dirty voter roll: Getting off isn’t so easy](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY MIKE O'DONNELL, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
_A deep dive into Colorado's voter registration data reveals a roll bloated with dead voters, out-of-state movers, and phantom registrants — while the Secretary of State's office pays $50,000 a year to a partisan nonprofit to do cleanup work that could be done for $60 a month._
* Colorado's voter roll lists 1,569 centenarian registrants despite only an estimated 890 centenarians actually living in the state, including a purported 127-year-old registrant and 20 registrants older than the oldest known Coloradan alive — a clear signal that deceased voters are not being removed in a timely manner despite state law requiring monthly death-record reporting.
* There are currently 25,464 active-status registrants who have filed change-of-address forms confirming they moved out of state — some as far back as 2022 — yet remain on Colorado's active voter roll, and all 25,464 would have had primary ballots mailed to their old Colorado addresses.
* Rather than directly cross-referencing the voter roll against the postal service's NCOA database for $60 a month, the Secretary of State pays approximately $50,000 annually to ERIC — a partisan nonprofit — while county clerks are legally barred from using readily available county assessor property records that would instantly flag voters who've sold their homes and moved away.

**[READ MORE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
|

**[The bonds that cannot be dissolved](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**BY RMV EDITORIAL BOARD | COMMENTARY | JULY 5** _The Declaration of Independence opens by taking something apart. Before it reaches life, liberty and the pursuit of happiness, it lays out why one people must “dissolve the political bands” that tie them to another. The founding act is a break._
__
**[The creativity weapon: Loving the crooked man](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**BY DRAKE HUNTER | COMMENTARY | JULY 5** _When I was little, one of my favorite people ever was Grandma Ivy, still is. She wasn’t famous. She never stood behind a pulpit or wrote a book. But she was a superhero. During many of my toddler and elementary years, she was my guardian, my safe place, and my greatest teacher. Like so many grandmothers, she had a way of turning ordinary moments into lasting memories._
__
**[The American Dream still depends on rewarding hard work](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)****BY GABE EVANS | COMMENTARY | JULY 3**
_When our founding fathers signed the Declaration of Independence, they envisioned a nation that could stand the test of time. A United States of America that not only encouraged freedom and independent thought, but that structurally safeguarded it. They believed in a nation defined by liberty, opportunity, personal responsibility, and an enduring love of country._

Dear Peter,

When I say "I'll protect you, not the system," here's what I mean.

Agriculture is one of the most important industries in the 5th District and across South Carolina. It powers our economy, feeds
our families, and supports hundreds of thousands of jobs.

But behind every acre of farmland is a family carrying an incredible burden.

Farming is one of the toughest professions in America. Farmers face relentless uncertainty from droughts, rising fuel and
equipment costs, volatile commodity prices, and mounting financial pressure. Many carry the weight of generational farms and debts
while working long hours in isolation.

The human toll is real.

Studies have found that U.S. farmers are significantly more likely to die by suicide than workers in many other occupations. This
is a heartbreaking reminder that when farming struggles, it's not just an economic issue. It's a family issue.

Over the past two years, South Carolina farmers have suffered nearly $700 million in losses.

That's why I recently fought for a $35 million farm relief proviso, which passed the South Carolina Senate unanimously.

This isn't new government spending. It simply redirects existing dollars from an economic development slush fund to the people who
grow our food and keep our rural communities strong.

Under this proviso, eligible farmers can receive grants of up to $135,000 to help weather a difficult season.

Protecting taxpayers means saying no to wasteful spending. Protecting the people means standing with hardworking families when
they need it most.

That's what I mean when I say: I'll protect you, not the system.

In service,

Wes

clean_body: Behind every acre of farmland is a family carrying an incredible burden. [] [] Donate [] | Facebook [] | X / Twitter [] | Instagram Donate [] Facebook [] X/Twitter [] Instagram [] Dear Peter, When I say "I'll protect you, not the system," here's what I mean. Agriculture is one of the most important industries in the 5th District and across South Carolina. It powers our economy, feeds our families, and supports hundreds of thousands of jobs. But behind every acre of farmland is a family carrying an incredible burden. Farming is one of the toughest professions in America. Farmers face relentless uncertainty from droughts, rising fuel and equipment costs, volatile commodity prices, and mounting financial pressure. Many carry the weight of generational farms and debts while working long hours in isolation. The human toll is real. Studies have found that U.S. farmers are significantly more likely to die by suicide than workers in many other occupations. This is a heartbreaking reminder that when farming struggles, it's not just an economic issue. It's a family issue. Over the past two years, South Carolina farmers have suffered nearly $700 million in losses. That's why I recently fought for a $35 million farm relief proviso, which passed the South Carolina Senate unanimously. This isn't new government spending. It simply redirects existing dollars from an economic development slush fund to the people who grow our food and keep our rural communities strong. Under this proviso, eligible farmers can receive grants of up to $135,000 to help weather a difficult season. Protecting taxpayers means saying no to wasteful spending. Protecting the people means standing with hardworking families when they need it most. That's what I mean when I say: I'll protect you, not the system. Patriot,

It's been over a year since President Trump pardoned us J6 prisoners.

But even with the pardons, you may not realize what life is like for many J6ers...

**Some are homeless to this day. Some can 't get a job because of the time they've spent in jail. Many are struggling to return to some semblance of a normal life.**

They have been separated from their families for years. They have had their rights stripped from them. They can't vote. They can't own a firearm.

Not only are these men and women patriots, but they come from all walks of life -- law enforcement, veterans, white-collar professionals, blue-collar workers, and all races and religions.

_And they were hunted down in a political persecution that denied them their constitutional rights. _

So what comes next for J6ers?

There are nearly 1,600 Americans who need to rebuild their lives. That's exactly what Stand in the Gap Foundation is helping them do.

[Patriot, as a personal favor to me, can you please send an urgent donation of $10 or more? Stand in the Gap Foundation originally started to help reunite families with a loved one incarcerated due to J6. Now, our focus is on helping those J6ers navigate the challenging process of re-entry into society after being incarcerated.

We are committed to providing comprehensive, practical support to ensure that each individual can rebuild their life with dignity, hope, and purpose.

Our mission is deeply rooted in the conviction that legal forgiveness is only the beginning. We want to give J6ers the support to fully reintegrate into their communities with the strength to start anew.

clean_body: It's been over a year since President Trump pardoned us J6 prisoners. Patriot, It's been over a year since President Trump pardoned us J6 prisoners. But even with the pardons, you may not realize what life is like for many J6ers... Some are homeless to this day. Some can 't get a job because of the time they've spent in jail. Many are struggling to return to some semblance of a normal life. They have been separated from their families for years. They have had their rights stripped from them. They can't vote. They can't own a firearm. Not only are these men and women patriots, but they come from all walks of life -- law enforcement, veterans, white-collar professionals, blue-collar workers, and all races and religions. And they were hunted down in a political persecution that denied them their constitutional rights. So what comes next for J6ers? There are nearly 1,600 Americans who need to rebuild their lives. That's exactly what Stand in the Gap Foundation is helping them do. Stand in the Gap Foundation originally started to help reunite families with a loved one incarcerated due to J6. Now, our focus is on helping those J6ers navigate the challenging process of re-entry into society after being incarcerated. We are committed to providing comprehensive, practical support to ensure that each individual can rebuild their life with dignity, hope, and purpose. Our mission is deeply rooted in the conviction that legal forgiveness is only the beginning. We want to give J6ers the support to fully reintegrate into their communities with the strength to start anew. name: America Fitzpatrick, LCV
subject: Trump sold 70,000 acres in the Arctic Refuge — we need your help
body:
We need your help to ensure no rigs ever touch the ground.

If you are unable to see the message below, [click here to view](https://links.messages.lcv.org/servlet/MailView?ms=MTM4MjUxMjYS1&r=NjA3MDU0MTAzNTc3S0&j=MjUwMDA0NjY4NAS2&mt=1&rt=0).
| | | |
---
|
* * *
---
| | | | DEVELOPING... the Trump administration just sold off tens of thousands of acres of the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge to oil and gas companies. Trump has promised to “drill, baby, drill” from the extraordinary place the Gwich’in people call “the sacred place where life begins.”
---
| | **We’re calling on our members for help.** Sales like these have happened before, but there’s never been drilling in the Arctic Refuge because the environmental movement has been able to break through to major oil companies. This sale had only 2 bidders — no major oil companies — and one was the Alaska state-run corporation that stepped in due to lack of competition. But that doesn’t mean we can let up the pressure — we need your help to continue to hold the line in one of the last wild places on Earth.
---
| | **Please, Peter:**[**Renew your LCV membership for $15 during our Summer Membership Drive to TRIPLE your impact to protect irreplaceable wilderness like the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge >>**](https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/2zZrMN3aD-)
---
| |
## _**LCV 2026 SUMMER MEMBERSHIP DRIVE**_
_**MEMBER STATUS**_
---
| |
---
| | **Supporter Record:** Peter Willis
**Match Status:** [_**_TRIPLE MATCH ACTIVE >>_**_](https://links.messages.lcv.) **Deadline:** July 31, 2026
**Membership Drive Goal:** 5,000 membership contributions **Member Status:**[**_EXPIRED — renew your membership today for $15 >>_**](https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/VXb6sXjg~)
---
| | The Arctic National Wildlife Refuge is home to polar bears, millions of migratory birds, and the porcupine caribou herd that has sustained the Gwich’in people for generations. For decades, the Gwich’in have led the movement to keep the Arctic Refuge free from corporate greed and extraction — no drilling, no development.
---
| | But Trump’s vision for the Refuge is clear: _turn this sacred land into an industrial oil field. _
---
| | **Here's the thing though:** This won’t be the last lease sale for the Refuge. We need to continue to remind these companies that drilling in the Refuge is financially risky, wildly unpopular, and incompatible with a rapidly changing Arctic.
---
| | We need to keep organizing and keep public pressure up. That means supporting Indigenous and frontline communities, holding oil companies and members of Congress accountable, and mobilizing as many pro-climate and pro-clean energy voters as possible ahead of November’s midterm elections.
---
| | But none of this works without you, Peter. We can’t afford to sit this one out.
---
| | | [RENEW YOUR MEMBERSHIP >>](https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/NvbyBGEP~)
---
| | Thank you for everything you do to protect public lands, Peter. Together, we can make sure that Trump greed never breaks the ice in the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge.
---
| | | | America Fitzpatrick
Conservation Program Director
League of Conservation Voters

I am a patriot. To me, that means loving this country enough to serve it, grapple with the truth about where we fall short, and fight for every American. subject: “Media capture” and why we should worry about it
body:
[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/398?t=1008&refcode=20260707_MJ&akid=122%2E344797%2ECgwbq6 ]COURIER Newsroom

Hi Peter — Mark Jacob here, contributor at COURIER.

I'm increasingly worried about "media capture": when billionaires buy up
mass-communication companies and use them to disinform the public and prop
up a strongman leader. In the U.S., the trend is disturbing.

Last month the Murdoch family's Fox Corp. moved to buy Roku, used by 100
million households. Days later, Trump's Justice Department fast-tracked
the pro-Trump Ellison family's bid for Warner Bros. Discovery, CNN's
parent company. The Ellisons already grabbed a slice of TikTok, took over
CBS News, and installed Bari Weiss to push pro-Trump spin. This is media
capture in open collaboration with the regime.

I recently wrote about what the CNN takeover will mean, why MS NOW is
rising, and NPR's embarrassing week.

[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/398?t=1003&refcode=20260707_MJ&akid=122%2E344797%2ECgwbq6 ]Before you read on, I hope you'll consider supporting COURIER.
Independent journalism matters when powerful media outlets are lining up
behind Trump and MAGA.

Thanks for reading,
Mark Jacob
COURIER Contributor

--------------------------------------------------------------------------

[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/398?t=1004&refcode=20260707_MJ&akid=122%2E344797%2ECgwbq6 ][IMG]

While CNN may get worse, MS NOW is getting better
We should worry about "media capture" that empowers the Trump regime
By Mark Jacob

I'm increasingly worried about "media capture."

That's when rich people buy up mass-communication companies and use them
to disinform the public and empower a strongman leader.

In the United States, the trend is disturbing.

Last month, the right-wing Murdoch family's Fox Corp. announced plans to
buy streaming TV platform Roku, which is used by 100 million American
households. Also last month, the U.S. "Justice" Department fast-tracked
the pro-Trump Ellison family's bid to acquire Warner Bros. Discovery,
parent company of CNN. The Ellisons have already gained a share of TikTok
with Trump's help and taken over CBS News, where they hired right-wing
favorite Bari Weiss to promote pro-Trump disinformation.

Clearly, the Ellison family is pursuing media capture in collaboration
with the regime.

[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/398?t=1005&refcode=20260707_MJ&akid=122%2E344797%2ECgwbq6 ]DONATE

Trump's DOJ approved Ellison-owned Paramount's bid to buy Warner Bros.
Discovery, and thus take control of CNN, before its own staff had a chance
to oppose the deal on antitrust grounds. State attorneys general and/or
European regulators could still block the sale, but the smart money says
the Ellisons' takeover is a done deal.

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is cheerleading for it. In March, he
denounced "more fake news from CNN" and said, "The sooner David Ellison
takes over that network, the better."

So what would that mean for CNN's coverage?

I predict a slow slide to the right. CNN reports sharply about Trump at
times, and does a good job of running clips of his past statements to
demonstrate his hypocrisy. But it generally stops short of the obvious
sweeping conclusion that he's building an authoritarian government.
Journalists like Jim Acosta and John Harwood who were really hardnosed
about Trump have left the network. Meanwhile, MAGA liar Scott Jennings
remains on CNN's payroll.

Some CNN journalists seem worried about the prospect of pro-Trump bias,
especially if Bari Weiss' role expands to cover CNN too. Scott Pelley was
fired at CBS after accusing Weiss of "murdering '60 Minutes.'" He said she
pressured the program to make Minnesota protesters look "more violent" and
to report that shooting victim Renee Good drove her car toward an
immigration agent when she didn't.

The New York Post's Charles Gasparino reported that CNN's staff is "in a
panic" over the likely takeover, and he quoted an unnamed Paramount
insider as saying, "Yes, I know people are scared but we're looking to
produce a news product that appeals to 70% of the country that is either
center left or center right. Why be scared of that?"

David Ellison likes to cite that 70% figure, but it's wrong. Polls show
that only about 40% of American adults put themselves in the center. But
whatever the number, a more legitimate approach would be to avoid
pandering to the supposed center and instead "center" the truth. Report
the facts. Keep liars off the air.

I don't expect that to happen at CNN. Nor do I anticipate a dramatic lurch
to the right. That was Weiss' big mistake at CBS, costing it both
credibility and viewership. I suspect the Ellisons have learned their
lesson and will turn the dial only slightly to the right, allowing a few
more Republicans to tell a few more lies.

One of CNN's strengths is its international coverage, and that may face
the greatest threat. The Ellisons are major supporters of Israel under
Benjamin Netanyahu's leadership, as is Weiss. Also, if the Ellisons'
Paramount buys WBD, 15% of the combined company will be owned by the Saudi
sovereign wealth fund. Yes, the people who murdered journalist Jamal
Khashoggi.

CNN is sometimes disappointing now. It's likely to get worse.

[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/398?t=1006&refcode=20260707_MJ&akid=122%2E344797%2ECgwbq6 ]DONATE

Now the good news

Counterbalancing the troubling prospects for CNN is what is happening
every day on MS NOW: hard-hitting, well-focused, fact-based news.

Since the former MSNBC separated from NBC last October and changed its
name to MS NOW, it has found its footing as a major pro-democracy voice in
our country. While other networks and the New York Times clutch their
pearls and say Trump is "testing norms," MS NOW is calling out corruption
and authoritarianism. It calls lies "lies."

But it would be wrong to think of MS NOW as just the liberal flipside of
Fox News. MS NOW is focused on real issues that matter to people's lives.
Fox is focused on culture clashes to instill fear and hatred. Also, and
this is most important, MS NOW seeks to convey the truth, unlike Fox,
which routinely twists the facts to mislead its viewers.

MS NOW features some of the best journalists in the business. Nicolle
Wallace's concentration on the threat of a dictatorship reflects a depth
of understanding often lacking in corporate media. Jacob Soboroff, a
leading reporter on the abuses of Trump's immigration crackdown, has a new
weekend show. Carol Leonnig regularly breaks news on national security and
law enforcement, while Lisa Rubin deftly explains complex court cases.

The likely decline of CNN and the growing influence of MS NOW are
demonstrated by legal affairs correspondent Paula Reid leaving CNN amid
reports that her next newsroom will be at MS NOW.

I still have problems with the self-indulgent Joe Scarborough on MS NOW's
"Morning Joe," but in general the network is a smart news operation that
respects its audience. We need more like it.

This week's media atrocity

NPR embarrassed itself with Nina Totenberg's false report that Justice
Samuel Alito was retiring. Totenberg called it "the worst professional
mistake of my more than 50 years in journalism." But I think it was the

Thanks for reading, Mark Jacob COURIER Contributor [ ][IMG] While CNN may get worse, MS NOW is getting better We should worry about "media capture" that empowers the Trump regime By Mark Jacob I'm increasingly worried about "media capture." That's when rich people buy up mass-communication companies and use them to disinform the public and empower a strongman leader. In the United States, the trend is disturbing. Last month, the right-wing Murdoch family's Fox Corp. announced plans to buy streaming TV platform Roku, which is used by 100 million American households. Also last month, the U.S. "Justice" Department fast-tracked the pro-Trump Ellison family's bid to acquire Warner Bros. Discovery, parent company of CNN. The Ellisons have already gained a share of TikTok with Trump's help and taken over CBS News, where they hired right-wing favorite Bari Weiss to promote pro-Trump disinformation. Clearly, the Ellison family is pursuing media capture in collaboration with the regime. [ ]DONATE Trump's DOJ approved Ellison-owned Paramount's bid to buy Warner Bros. Discovery, and thus take control of CNN, before its own staff had a chance to oppose the deal on antitrust grounds. State attorneys general and/or European regulators could still block the sale, but the smart money says the Ellisons' takeover is a done deal. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is cheerleading for it. In March, he denounced "more fake news from CNN" and said, "The sooner David Ellison takes over that network, the better." So what would that mean for CNN's coverage? I predict a slow slide to the right. CNN reports sharply about Trump at times, and does a good job of running clips of his past statements to demonstrate his hypocrisy. But it generally stops short of the obvious sweeping conclusion that he's building an authoritarian government. Journalists like Jim Acosta and John Harwood who were really hardnosed about Trump have left the network. Meanwhile, MAGA liar Scott Jennings remains on CNN's payroll. Some CNN journalists seem worried about the prospect of pro-Trump bias, especially if Bari Weiss' role expands to cover CNN too. Scott Pelley was fired at CBS after accusing Weiss of "murdering '60 Minutes.'" He said she pressured the program to make Minnesota protesters look "more violent" and to report that shooting victim Renee Good drove her car toward an immigration agent when she didn't. The New York Post's Charles Gasparino reported that CNN's staff is "in a panic" over the likely takeover, and he quoted an unnamed Paramount insider as saying, "Yes, I know people are scared but we're looking to produce a news product that appeals to 70% of the country that is either center left or center right. Why be scared of that?" David Ellison likes to cite that 70% figure, but it's wrong. Polls show that only about 40% of American adults put themselves in the center. But whatever the number, a more legitimate approach would be to avoid pandering to the supposed center and instead "center" the truth. Report the facts. Keep liars off the air. I don't expect that to happen at CNN. Nor do I anticipate a dramatic lurch to the right. That was Weiss' big mistake at CBS, costing it both credibility and viewership. I suspect the Ellisons have learned their lesson and will turn the dial only slightly to the right, allowing a few more Republicans to tell a few more lies. One of CNN's strengths is its international coverage, and that may face the greatest threat. The Ellisons are major supporters of Israel under Benjamin Netanyahu's leadership, as is Weiss. Also, if the Ellisons' Paramount buys WBD, 15% of the combined company will be owned by the Saudi sovereign wealth fund. Yes, the people who murdered journalist Jamal Khashoggi. Carol Leonnig regularly breaks news on national security and law enforcement, while Lisa Rubin deftly explains complex court cases. The likely decline of CNN and the growing influence of MS NOW are demonstrated by legal affairs correspondent Paula Reid leaving CNN amid reports that her next newsroom will be at MS NOW. Four conservative members of the US Supreme Court just said that birthright citizenship should be stripped away, despite the Constitution's guarantees.
Worse yet: all 6 of the Republican Justices on the Court decided to blow open a devastating loophole that will now allow the super rich and billionaire political donors to coordinate spending unlimited sums of cash with candidates for public office.
The loophole is an arcane procedure called a "coordinated party expenditure" that now can be used to funnel unlimited cash through official party committees straight to candidates. Before the Court's ruling, these coordinated expenditures were subject to legal limits enforced by the FEC.
Justice Elena Kagan summed up how corrupt the Court's decision was in her dissent: "With no limits on coordinated expenditures, the party can serve as the candidate's checking account."

Peter,

It's been over a year since President Trump pardoned us J6 prisoners.

But even with the pardons, you may not realize what life is like for many J6ers...

**Some are homeless to this day. Some can 't get a job because of the time they've spent in jail. Many are struggling to return to some semblance of a normal life.**

They have been separated from their families for years. They have had their rights stripped from them. They can't vote. They can't own a firearm.

Not only are these men and women patriots, but they come from all walks of life -- law enforcement, veterans, white-collar professionals, blue-collar workers, and all races and religions.

_And they were hunted down in a political persecution that denied them their constitutional rights. _

So what comes next for J6ers?

There are nearly 1,600 Americans who need to rebuild their lives. That's exactly what Stand in the Gap Foundation is helping them do.

[Peter, as a personal favor to me, can you please send an urgent donation of $10 or more? I am hoping to get 100 supporters to help us in our mission to rebuild the lives of J6ers who need us now more than ever.](http://links.itsourgreatamerica.com/u/click?_t=442fb7cf105f4725a8bda0b6bcffc1bd&_m=d4f32a6a58824d1a9bb9730e065f7cee&_e=rda6VwzBUVsxs9MqUTwXQgi4Ab1YNQKfoePqKl5-29s0mNNtLbgjVGQElNXlnZUn4JUqhPbsrXodb_ERgqvz5-D__j5RFqiX4KnaKMGd72_d3yTj1UNhMnd7hPZxIwUNw2zFb1EgXQZ7SG5o005xhO9kAr8VYwxhaFbA2sf7Jyk8T_1xsgR64-QvIgEXaVp58Jv1P8V_unj46LasR1qooJwQQ961S9fSOoascZFvquDpjOGDbr7Doa-3saUx_xljnkddk13N9pWHAlpxGEePZOxZixNfWl5iQ_cx-tZEQkj6RSnqMMKYiHQx4t_flpbfkOhmG1MXnnNwomx67HRWbDF5Nm-q4ypve2KLv9SSZOJO9u5gc75DXm37Eje_N5fghhDIhDBvFZ3K9IJrNtaF4QGdgiid9FxJEiFaceEijX6SB9ucyUMiUXQ1kv0cOLaMsrQHOgE_aFQrfM026DLYTemRDkRFF7FLRmucyZpA5bdYHSlTjEpp2LWw4hLE3OQ0D5Tueko1DxBGTsxlqe7-GeirnJG5Z0ZLgHUd7XplJL60dpAr6hCbspA_vgJnmt8I2cKtRuXr8N_s0clOQueEG8bAnLKHVtGZWkL7Rdg15HDAuWSM8tyaVPLS0OSPoGr5)

Stand in the Gap Foundation originally started to help reunite families with a loved one incarcerated due to J6. Now, our focus is on helping those J6ers navigate the challenging process of re-entry into society after being incarcerated.

We are committed to providing comprehensive, practical support to ensure that each individual can rebuild their life with dignity, hope, and purpose.

Our mission is deeply rooted in the conviction that legal forgiveness is only the beginning. We want to give J6ers the support to fully reintegrate into their communities with the strength to start anew.

clean_body: It's been over a year since President Trump pardoned us J6 prisoners. Peter, It's been over a year since President Trump pardoned us J6 prisoners. But even with the pardons, you may not realize what life is like for many J6ers... Some are homeless to this day. Some can 't get a job because of the time they've spent in jail. Many are struggling to return to some semblance of a normal life. They have been separated from their families for years. They have had their rights stripped from them. They can't vote. They can't own a firearm. Not only are these men and women patriots, but they come from all walks of life -- law enforcement, veterans, white-collar professionals, blue-collar workers, and all races and religions. And they were hunted down in a political persecution that denied them their constitutional rights. So what comes next for J6ers? There are nearly 1,600 Americans who need to rebuild their lives. That's exactly what Stand in the Gap Foundation is helping them do. Stand in the Gap Foundation originally started to help reunite families with a loved one incarcerated due to J6. Now, our focus is on helping those J6ers navigate the challenging process of re-entry into society after being incarcerated. We are committed to providing comprehensive, practical support to ensure that each individual can rebuild their life with dignity, hope, and purpose. Our mission is deeply rooted in the conviction that legal forgiveness is only the beginning. We want to give J6ers the support to fully reintegrate into their communities with the strength to start anew. Surprisingly, there are very few resources for people who are released from prison, particularly if they are conservative or America First activists. While some J6ers come from families with means, most do not. We were founded to "stand in the gap" for those in prison and those navigating life after incarceration. We want them to know that they are not forgotten. This begins by providing housing and vehicles, counseling, and confidential peer support; the tools needed for healing and reintegration. subject: A conservative news outlet just endorsed our opponent

body:
The Democratic and Republican establishment are terrified of our movement.
#
Peter,
The _Detroit News_ just endorsed out-of-touch multimillionaire incumbent Rep. Shri Thanedar in Michigan’s 13th district ahead of the August 4th primary.
He claims it’s because he’s “stood up to Trump and fought for” the people he represents, but here’s why the conservative news outlet _actually_ endorsed him over our progressive challenger, Donavan McKinney:
**"He's a reliable supporter of Israel."**
**"The threat of socialism to the American system & prosperity is real. Michigan should not contribute another member to Congress's growing socialist caucus."**
The first point is true: Shri went from being a so-called “progressive” candidate who AIPAC spent against when he first ran for Congress to being endorsed by them, accepting their campaign checks, receiving millions in support from affiliated PACs, and going on AIPAC-sponsored trips to Israel.
**AIPAC has bought Shri’s loyalty. In fact, so have Big Tech, ICE contractors, and other corporate lobbies and megadonors.**
Donavan’s loyalty is to the people of the Mighty 13th. Unlike Shri, he doesn’t take a cent from AIPAC or corporate PACs, and he’s lived the most pressing problems his community faces: eviction, homelessness, watching his mom work multiple jobs to put food on the table, and suffering from the same asthmatic cough his family members and neighbors developed from air pollution.
Just like the rest of our 2026 slate, **Donavan is ready to fight for the working class by supporting the bold changes we deserve and need:** Medicare for All, housing for all, union jobs and higher wages, environmental justice, and an end to forever wars and genocide.
And the second point? It further goes to show that both the Democratic AND Republican establishment are _terrified_ of the progressive, people-powered movement we are building in Congress.
**[We just unseated an AIPAC and corporate-backed Do-Nothing Democrat in Denver. Help us do it again in Detroit next month by supporting Donavan and Justice Democrats with a split donation now!](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260707-1-dm.nEQhWi&refcode=em20260707-37997&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=2&akid=37997%2E1203867%2EQOWWgY)**

In solidarity,
Justice Democrats

Just like the rest of our 2026 slate, Donavan is ready to fight for the working class by supporting the bold changes we deserve and need: Medicare for All, housing for all, union jobs and higher wages, environmental justice, and an end to forever wars and genocide. And the second point? It further goes to show that both the Democratic AND Republican establishment are terrified of the progressive, people-powered movement we are building in Congress. Peter Willis,

Last night, Our Revolution withdrew our endorsement of Graham Platner. The
allegations against him are serious and he must step aside.

We also told the Democratic establishment, in no uncertain terms: this is
NOT your opening. Remember: Progressives overwhelmingly won the primary. A
progressive MUST be on the ballot.

not corporate interests. But now, we’re at a critical crossroads with just
DAYS before the ballot deadline — and we’re rallying behind Troy Jackson
to replace Platner. He’s a logger, a union leader, and the former
president of the Maine State Senate who led Bernie’s campaign for
President twice in Maine and had Bernie’s backing in his run for Governor.

Troy knows what it means to put in a hard day’s work and never back down
from a fight. And he just filed the paperwork to run for this Senate seat
and fight for working people in Washington.

But if we don’t come together right now, we risk ceding this race to the
Democratic establishment — and we refuse to let that happen. Our
organizing machine sprang into action last night, and now, we urgently
need resources to unleash our Citizen Action Team in support of Troy and
build an army of grassroots volunteers across the state.

name: Pramila Jayapal
subject: 252 new Americans
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
252 new Americans took the Oath of Allegiance on July 4th.
# [](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/892?refcode=em20260707-6439-footer&t=1&akid=6439%2E420207%2EC82b23)
Hi Peter,
This past weekend, as our nation celebrated its 250th anniversary, I had the incredible honor of speaking at a naturalization ceremony in Seattle, where 252 people became the newest citizens of the United States.
There could not have been a more fitting way to mark this milestone, because **immigrants have always been at the heart of America’s story** — a story that is never ending and continues to be shaped by every generation that chooses to build a better future here.
America’s strength has **_always**_ come from people who bring their own experiences, cultures, and dreams, and who choose to build a better future together.
It took me 17 years to become a U.S. citizen. As one of only about two dozen naturalized citizens serving in Congress, I can’t forget what a privilege it is to serve this country, nor the responsibility that comes with it.
America is a nation built on a radical promise: that all people are created equal, with the right to life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness. Together, we are called to help build a more perfect union together.
That is how we've made progress throughout our history — by people coming together to expand opportunity, protect our freedoms, and build a more just and inclusive nation, even when the odds were high and the journey was hard.
**And there is still more work to do in this American project. That’s the work I’ve dedicated my life to, and it’s the work I’ll continue to do every day in Congress.**
[**If you’re able, will you chip in $3 today to help me continue fighting for an America that lives up to its highest ideals?**](https://act.pramilaforcongress.com/go/47393?c0=pj-em-20260707.kwxPRk&refcode=em20260707-6439&amount=3&t=2&akid=6439%2E420207%2EC82b23)

Thank you,
Pramila Jayapal

Peter, Yesterday, after a morning run in the woods, I recorded a quick video because I felt like I needed to be honest with you. I was sweaty, tired, and still catching my breath, but I did not want to start the day without saying what has been sitting heavy on my heart: **I’ve been struggling lately. If Trump has his way, the Pax Americana, won through trillions of dollars of American treasure, decades of American labor, and hundreds of thousands of American lives, will end.
#
Donald Trump just renewed his demand for control of Greenland. He made these demands at a NATO summit, held to bolster ties with our NATO allies, as we face threats from Russia, China, and a world Trump himself has thrown into chaos.
His “peace deal” with Iran teeters on the brink of collapse. The last war isn’t even over, and Trump’s already salivating at the prospect of the next one.
NATO is the most powerful military alliance in the history of mankind, and has allowed for unprecedented prosperity and peace. The US defeated fascism and liberated the world at the cost of hundreds of thousands of American lives in the Second World War. In the decades since we've spent uncountable sums of money constructing a new global security framework with freedom, democracy, and the United States at the center of it.
If Trump has his way, the Pax Americana, won through trillions of dollars of American treasure, decades of American labor, and hundreds of thousands of American lives, will end. NATO will end. And we will have more in common with the Russians and Chinese than with our closest allies.
It is impossible to overstate how critically important the elections this November are. If Trump holds majorities in Congress he will drag us into another war. If we take back the House and Senate, we can stop him.
Peter, we need you. We need to raise millions of dollars to defeat MAGA candidates up and down the ballot and replace them with principled leaders who will stop Trump when it matters most.

Peter, Imagine what Election Day this November could look like if Trump and his MAGA cronies get their way — and then make a donation today to support our critical work standing in the way of this nightmare:
* Millions of voters could be prevented from receiving a mail-in ballot they rely on if they happen to live in a state that did not cave to pressure from Trump’s Justice Department to turn over their voter rolls.
* ICE and DHS agents could be deployed at polling sites to intimidate voters.
* At the polls, eligible voters would have to show proof of citizenship to cast their ballots. Married women who changed their last names would need to track down birth certificates and marriage licenses. This also affects millions of people who don’t have their “papers” readily at hand, from people with disabilities to rural voters to those who’ve lost possessions in moves or natural disasters.
* After votes are counted, pro-Democratic results could be investigated by federal authorities over nonsensical “election fraud” allegations, simply because the administration doesn’t like the outcome.

**Right now, Trump is blocking critical, bipartisan housing legislation in an attempt to pressure Congress to pass his anti-voter wish list. clean_body: Together, we can stand in their way and ensure the will of the people prevails. | Peter, Imagine what Election Day this November could look like if Trump and his MAGA cronies get their way — and then make a donation today to support our critical work standing in the way of this nightmare: Millions of voters could be prevented from receiving a mail-in ballot they rely on if they happen to live in a state that did not cave to pressure from Trump’s Justice Department to turn over their voter rolls. ICE and DHS agents could be deployed at polling sites to intimidate voters. At the polls, eligible voters would have to show proof of citizenship to cast their ballots. Married women who changed their last names would need to track down birth certificates and marriage licenses. This also affects millions of people who don’t have their “papers” readily at hand, from people with disabilities to rural voters to those who’ve lost possessions in moves or natural disasters. After votes are counted, pro-Democratic results could be investigated by federal authorities over nonsensical “election fraud” allegations, simply because the administration doesn’t like the outcome. Right now, Trump is blocking critical, bipartisan housing legislation in an attempt to pressure Congress to pass his anti-voter wish list. We are the grassroots movement standing in his way — and we can't afford to take our eye off the ball. = | = We’re already seeing some of these threats come to fruition: Last month, we witnessed immigration agents confront a poll worker in Upstate New York. Anti-democracy extremists are raiding election offices, questioning local officials, and demanding ballots in Georgia, Michigan, Wisconsin, and Arizona in an effort to relitigate debunked conspiracy theories about Trump’s 2020 loss. This is an alarming trend that threatens the very foundation of our democracy. = Thank you, Claire Low Director of Political and Campaigns National Democratic Redistricting Committee = = | | Paid for by the National Democratic Redistricting Committee, John Bisognano, President. | | | | | | | ---|---|---|---|---|---|--- National Democratic Redistricting Committee 712 H St NE, #25 Washington, DC 20002 United States if you'd like to receive fewer emails from the NDRC. Will’s climate activism began at age twelve, when he first learned about climate change.
**He co-founded the Sunrise Movement and started the nation’s first campus fossil fuel divestment campaign while a student in college.** His coalition-building work for the Green New Deal has _already resulted_ in real policy outcomes, like portions of the Build Back Better plan and the Inflation Reduction Act.
He’s also put his body on the line to protest pipeline projects. In fact, his arrest record looks a lot like mine!
As with many progressive, pro-planet candidates, Will’s in a tough primary that will determine who goes on to flip this now-red seat blue. He opposes fossil fuel expansion, and he doesn’t take a dime from Big Oil.
**The stakes couldn’t be higher for a district like this, where legacy industrial pollution and even two major Superfund sites have already endangered too many.**

Team,

Over the next few months, you're going to get a lot of emails asking for your financial support ahead of the election.

This isn't one of those emails. Today, I just want to hear from you.

Too many politicians stop listening the moment they get to Washington. They take their cues from corporate donors and lobbyists, not the people they're supposed to serve — and after a while, they forget who they work for entirely. That's exactly the kind of representation I'm running to replace.

I don't answer to corporate PACs. I never have, and I never will. I answer to you. And that means actually hearing what's on your mind — not telling you what to think.

## Celebrating America’s 250th!
---
|
---
[|
---](https://jonnyutah4congress.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=dc76e2ed74de192812d6308cf&id=4ddfab0dd9&e=c29ddb867a)
| |
The biggest 250th birthday party was right here in Utah! Crowds filled the streets of [Riverton](https://jonnyutah4congress.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=dc76e2ed74de192812d6308cf&id=f97b774acc&e=c29ddb867a), [Grantsville](https://jonnyutah4congress.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=dc76e2ed74de192812d6308cf&id=ac5353093f&e=c29ddb867a), and [Sandy](https://jonnyutah4congress.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=dc76e2ed74de192812d6308cf&id=96545e056b&e=c29ddb867a), dressed to the occasion and brought energy to match!
We had a great time celebrating America’s 250th this weekend. We were very happy to be out there supporting our fellow candidates [Benyde Walker](https://jonnyutah4congress.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=dc76e2ed74de192812d6308cf&id=1280932c21&e=c29ddb867a) and [Lillian Bowles](https://jonnyutah4congress.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=dc76e2ed74de192812d6308cf&id=4151d4112e&e=c29ddb867a). This is what collective unity looks and feels like, and we are here for all of it.

name: Wes Moore
subject: Cynicism and skepticism
body:
# [](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/8?t=1&akid=1597%2E1086043%2EJaIdTr)
Peter, I want to talk to the skeptics.
I get it. Politics has let a lot of people down. The cynicism is earned.
But here's what I've learned: skepticism is important, _as long as you make it your companion and not your captor._
I don't come from a political family. I don't think in political terms. I think in terms of results. And results are what we've delivered in Maryland.
Homicides down. Energy bills lower. Teacher vacancies cut in half. $10 billion in new private investment.
I'm not asking you to give up your skepticism. I'm asking you to channel it into something that actually changes things.
**[Can you chip in $5, or whatever you can today, and help us continue to deliver results for the people of Maryland?](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260707-1.3VZ928&refcode=em-20260707-1&t=2&akid=1597%2E1086043%2EJaIdTr)**
**[Donate $5 ››](https://act.wesmoore.com/go/417?c0=wes-em-20260707-1.3VZ928&amount=5&refcode=em-20260707-1&t=21&akid=1597%2E1086043%2EJaIdTr)**
The most powerful thing a skeptic can do is prove the cynics wrong.
– Wes Moore

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/134831054/632302517/-870569556?sourceid=1059415&refcode=WUEFES25_20260707_BelieveWomen_PL&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNRUwvMS84NzA2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhNjE3ZjZmZi01NzdhLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ogwq-romX0poz_y5UpP9Kz_rQrrIQPK_y_Z8SW44pUE=) Peter,

When allegations of sexual assault, abuse, or misconduct come to light, the response from our party should be clear: **We trust women. We stand with survivors. And we hold candidates accountable.**

The latest allegations against Graham Platner are horrifying. And they come after a long series of comments, actions, and allegations that raised serious concerns about his candidacy.

That is exactly why, when his disturbing comments minimizing sexual assault first came out, we warned it would be "the fastest way to hand Susan Collins a victory, should Platner advance in this race." When red flags are minimized, explained away, or treated as politically inconvenient, we end up here.

It's not enough to go off of vibes or who looks good on paper. Democrats have to ask who is actually prepared to lead, who has earned voters' trust, and who can win a general election — without asking women to ignore the warning signs.

Too often, men seeking power get the benefit of the doubt. Their records get excused. Serious concerns get dismissed as distractions. Women are asked to be patient, practical, and politically convenient — until the damage is impossible to ignore.

Meanwhile, women candidates are scrutinized at every turn. Their records, their families, their resumes, even their tone of voice — all of it is questioned before they're deemed "electable."

**That double standard is unacceptable.**

All candidates should be held to the same standard — and that standard cannot be lower for men seeking power than it is for women candidates every day. At EMILYs List, we know "electable" does not mean "excusable." Strong candidates don't need their red flags explained away. They are prepared, principled, and ready to fight for their communities.

Peter, women deserve leaders who respect us — in public, in private, and in the halls of power. And voters deserve candidates who meet that standard.

[**Will you donate today to help elect Democratic pro-choice women who are ready to lead with integrity and fight for their communities?**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/134831056/632302521/-870569556?sourceid=1059415&refcode=WUEFES25_20260707_BelieveWomen_PL&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNRUwvMS84NzA2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhNjE3ZjZmZi01NzdhLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ogwq-romX0poz_y5UpP9Kz_rQrrIQPK_y_Z8SW44pUE=) | [DONATE](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/134831059/632302523/1425818251?sourceid=1059415&refcode=WUEFES25_20260707_BelieveWomen_PL&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9UU00vVFNNRUwvMS84NzA2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhNjE3ZjZmZi01NzdhLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=ogwq-romX0poz_y5UpP9Kz_rQrrIQPK_y_Z8SW44pUE=)

clean_body: | = Peter, When allegations of sexual assault, abuse, or misconduct come to light, the response from our party should be clear: We trust women. We stand with survivors. And we hold candidates accountable. The latest allegations against Graham Platner are horrifying. And they come after a long series of comments, actions, and allegations that raised serious concerns about his candidacy. That is exactly why, when his disturbing comments minimizing sexual assault first came out, we warned it would be "the fastest way to hand Susan Collins a victory, should Platner advance in this race." When red flags are minimized, explained away, or treated as politically inconvenient, we end up here. It's not enough to go off of vibes or who looks good on paper. Democrats have to ask who is actually prepared to lead, who has earned voters' trust, and who can win a general election — without asking women to ignore the warning signs. Too often, men seeking power get the benefit of the doubt. Their records get excused. Serious concerns get dismissed as distractions. Women are asked to be patient, practical, and politically convenient — until the damage is impossible to ignore. Meanwhile, women candidates are scrutinized at every turn. Their records, their families, their resumes, even their tone of voice — all of it is questioned before they're deemed "electable." That double standard is unacceptable. All candidates should be held to the same standard — and that standard cannot be lower for men seeking power than it is for women candidates every day. At EMILYs List, we know "electable" does not mean "excusable." Strong candidates don't need their red flags explained away. They are prepared, principled, and ready to fight for their communities. Peter, women deserve leaders who respect us — in public, in private, and in the halls of power. And voters deserve candidates who meet that standard. = | = This is about more than one candidate or one race. It is about the standard we set — and whether we are willing to do the work to meet it. I am a proud member of Laguna Pueblo, and I carry with me the strength and resilience of generations of Pueblo women who refused to let their voices — or our people — be erased. They taught me that leadership means showing up for your community and making sure everyone has a seat at the table.
Their example gave me the courage to run for office, becoming one of the first Native American women elected to Congress and the first Native American Cabinet Secretary in our nation's history. **Now, I'm running to become the first Native American woman elected Governor in the United States — not just to make history, but to make a difference.**

We're making progress, friend. More and more people have a voice in the decisions that shape our future, and we're not giving up our seats at the table. I'm running because I believe every New Mexican deserves to be heard, especially when Washington gets it wrong, and I'll always stand up for working families, no matter who they are or where they live.
I want to leave the ladder down for the next generation of leaders and build a government that truly reflects and fights for the people it serves. But I can't do it without you, friend. [**Please, can I count on you to chip in $5 or more to help me fight for working families and deliver real progress for New Mexicans?**](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/12770?refcode=jtk989-fr-nd&t=7&akid=10882%2E400544%2Ezy9YsE)

Trump's latest judicial
nominee sat before the Senate Judiciary Committee — and refused to
acknowledge that the U.S. Capitol was attacked on January 6th.

This is Trump’s loyalty test. And Domenico passed.

Domenico is Trump's pick for the Tenth Circuit Court of Appeals — a
lifetime seat on a federal court covering six states. And his record on
the bench already tells you everything you need to know.

In eight separate cases, Domenico ruled that immigrants could be held in
ICE detention without a bond hearing. Not once, not twice — eight times,
he sided with the Trump administration's mass detention agenda.

His position is so extreme that it puts him at odds with every other
federal district judge in his own state.

This is who Trump wants shaping the law for a generation — and it’s
dangerous.

That's why Demand Justice PAC is sounding the alarm — on Domenico, on
every Trump loyalist rushed onto the federal bench, and on every senator
rubber-stamping all of it. We're tracking these nominees, exposing their
records, and pressuring senators to stop treating lifetime appointments
like a formality.

The courts are being stacked in real time. And if we don't step up now,
we'll be living with these consequences for decades.

name: Team Molder
subject: This is what good looks like.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Molder for Congress
body:
Every corner of TN-5 deserves this same commitment.

| | | | |
---
Friend,
Northside Square in Klondike is exactly what community progress looks like.
Neighbors gathering. Families putting down roots. Culture staying intact. A neighborhood that feels like home because a group of visionaries made the decision to invest in the people who live there. Memphis is doing something right, and it deserves a congressman who sees that and fights to replicate it everywhere.
Chaz has spent eight years proving that this works. Columbia is not the same city it was when he took office–downtown is thriving, small businesses are growing, and people feel like their community is worth investing in. I’m Dr. Annie Andrews, a pediatrician, a mom of three, and the Democrat running for U.S. Senate to defeat Republican Lindsey Graham in South Carolina.
If we flip this seat, we can end Lindsey Graham’s career and help Democrats retake the Senate, and expand the map for Democrats in future elections.
I know this won’t be easy. But I’ve treated kids who were shot, hospitalized, and failed by broken systems. Nothing about this moment feels optional.

Let me introduce myself.
I’ve spent nearly 20 years serving my community as a pediatrician, treating everything from asthma and violent trauma to the emotional toll of growing up in poverty.
I’ve seen what bad policy does to good families — and I’ve seen kids suffer because people like Lindsey Graham would rather protect their own power than protect children.
In 2022, after 15 years of working in hospitals, I ran for Congress because I knew our kids needed a voice in Washington. I lost — and I told my oldest daughter I wouldn’t run again.

And Lindsey Graham? He cheered.
The truth is, I’m scared. And I’m angry. And I’m done waiting.
So I’m stepping up — because our kids, and this country can’t afford another six years of Lindsey Graham.

Hi,
I’ll be honest: Deciding to throw my hat into this Senate race last summer wasn’t easy.
I thought long and hard about it, because it wasn’t a decision that just affected me. I knew it would touch my entire family and those closest to me – and it would require some sacrifice, lots of energy, and massive amounts of funding.
But when I saw all that was happening in Washington – the chaos, the cruelty, and the politicians rigging the system even further against working people – I knew I couldn’t sit on the sidelines.
I love Ohio. I love our people. And I won't let Jon Husted try to buy this seat and dictate our future.
**While Husted is proud to be on the side of Wall Street billionaires and special interests, I’m proud to have spent my life beating back these corrupt forces. I’ve spent it on picket lines, in union halls, and in conversation with everyday folks.**
I've always put Ohioans first – whether I was fighting for affordable health care or good-paying jobs, or saving Ohioans' pensions. I will stand by my record any day, and I’m determined to return to the Senate to do _even_ _more_.
**But I need your help to get there._[Polling shows this race within the margin of error, and the only way we can pull ahead is with your critical grassroots support. So please, will you chip in to my campaign today to flip Ohio and take back the Senate?](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/134831799/632304493/-1037742479?amounts=250,100,50,25,5&amount=5&refcode=jtk5197-fr-ndva&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1YjY3YWFjMC01YjdhLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=_FHbwk3P08Ptdp-ymjBCvGvwtGqsWNlwgsX1WK9uRvM=)_**

There's nobody fighting for Ohioans in the U.S. Senate right now, and I won't sit on the sidelines while working people get screwed over by large corporations and wealthy political donors.

If you work hard, you should be able to afford a decent life. But the reality is, life is too expensive. Costs are going up. Wages are staying stagnant. Working people are working harder than ever before, and they're not getting their share of the profit.

This campaign is all about changing that – and election analysts say we have a strong shot at winning in November.

But I'll need your help to pull it off: My opponent is a Washington insider being propped up by the Republican establishment, and he's got virtually unlimited resources.

But with the Q2 filing deadline behind us, it’s time to start spending. TV is still one of the best ways to reach voters in every corner of Wisconsin. And with the August 11 primary five weeks away, we want to do everything we can to win.

I was inside the Capitol when the mob broke through. I heard the shouting in the hallways. I watched my colleagues scramble for safety. | [ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/134832029/632305286/1922286040?amount=10&refcode=LOC_EM_FR_2026.07.07_Back-The-Bold-Split_B1_F1_S1_C1_90OP-NC_RS-T0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODg1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjNjRiMzg2Mi01ZjdhLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=EDoOgoq1n45JuL2DVB2GVzIf0xcCSeYRYmLiLiQ8ADI=) I was there on January 6th, 2021.

I was inside the Capitol when the mob broke through. I heard the shouting in the hallways. I watched my colleagues scramble for safety.
